It draws 3 (4 if upgraded) cards and makes you select 1 card in hand to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]]. == Interactions == === Order === * Selecting a card to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] happens ''after'' drawing, meaning that you can also choose one of the newly drawn cards to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]]. === Synergies === * {{C|Acrobatics}}'s [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] effect synergises with several [[Silent]] cards and relics: ==== Cards ==== * [[Keywords#Discard|Discarding]] {{C|Tactician}} or {{C|Reflex}} will immediately activate their effects. * {{C|Eviscerate}} is discounted by 1 {{Icon|GE}} '''Energy''' this turn. * {{C|Sneaky Strike}} will now refund 2 {{Icon|GE}} '''Energy''' if also played this turn. ==== Relics ==== * {{R|Tough Bandages}} will grant 3 {{KW|Block}}. * {{R|Tingsha}} will deal 3 damage to a random enemy. * {{R|Hovering Kite}} will generate 1 {{Icon|GE}} '''Energy''' if this is the first time a card has been [[Keywords#Discard|discarded]] this turn. === Neutral === * {{C|Acrobatics}} can also be used to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] cards with end-of-turn effects, like {{C|Burn}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}} such as {{C|Regret}}. {{SilentNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

title: Adrenaline
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox | Name = Adrenaline | Image = Green-Adrenaline.png | Color = Green | Type = Skill | Rarity = Rare | Cost = 0 | Description = Gain ({{Icon|GE}};{{Icon|GE}} {{Icon|GE}}).
Draw 2 cards.
{{KW|Exhaust}}. | GivesToPlayer = Draw, Energy, Exhaust }} {{C|Adrenaline}} is a 0 {{Icon|GE}}-cost, {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It draws 2 cards, generates 1 (2) {{Icon|GE}}, and {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausts}}. == Interactions == === Synergies === Adrenaline provides card draw and {{Icon|GE}} generation with no up front cost, and as such, can benefit nearly any deck to some degree. However, there are some cases where it is particularly useful: * Cards which benefit from having many '''cards in hand''', such as {{C|Calculated Gamble}} and {{C|Storm of Steel}}. * '''High cost cards''' which are important to play consistently, such as {{C|Nightmare}} and {{C|Wraith Form}}. * '''X-cost cards''' such as {{C|Malaise}} or {{C|Skewer}} * Having more Energy also benefit's Silent's other draw options, as you can pay for cards such as {{C|Acrobatics}} and {{C|Backflip}} while still having Energy for the cards they draw. * Decks that want to play '''many cards in one turn''', such as those making use of {{R|Shuriken}}, {{R|Kunai}}, {{R|Ornamental Fan}}, {{R|Nunchaku}}, or {{C|Panache}}. === Anti-Synergies === Given how many strategies can benefit from Adrenaline, it is actually easier to list things which ''don't'': * '''{{R|Snecko Eye}}''' often makes Adrenaline cost more than 0, reducing the {{Icon|GE}} it generates, and often even making it cost Energy. * '''{{R|Velvet Choker}}''' caps your turn at 6 card plays, preventing the sorts of big turns Adrenaline enables. * Similarly, '''{{C|Normality}}''' can cause issues with attempting big turns. This can be mitigated with ways to discard or exhaust the Normality, as well as by not playing Adrenaline as your third card for the turn. * Certain fights, most notably [[Gremlin Nob]], [[Chosen]], [[Time Eater]], and the [[Corrupt Heart]], have '''downsides to playing cards''' which may make it worthwhile not to play Adrenaline. {{SilentNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox | Name = All for One | Image = Blue-AllforOne.png | Color = Blue | Type = Attack | Rarity = Rare | Cost = 2 | Description = Deal (10;14) damage.
Put all cost 0 cards from your discard pile into your hand. }} {{C|All for One}} is a 2 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} Card. It deals 10 (14 if upgraded) damage, and it will put all 0-cost cards from your discard pile into your hand. 0 {{Icon|BE}} '''Energy''' does not have to be the base {{Icon|BE}}-cost of that card, as long as it costs 0 while in the discard pile, it will be put in hand by this card. {{C|All for One}} will not put all 0-cost cards from your discard pile into your hand if that amount would exceed the hand size limit. In that case, it will take the cards in the order they appear in the discard pile until your hand is full. == Interactions == === Order === * {{C|All for One}} will not count as part of the hand anymore by the time it brings back 0 {{Icon|BE}}-cost cards, meaning it does not count towards the hand size limit. === Synergies === * It synergizes with every 0-cost card, all of which that belong to the Defect listed below: ==== Cards ==== * {{C|Beam Cell}}, {{C|Claw}}, {{C|Go for the Eyes}}, {{C|Steam Barrier}}, {{C|TURBO}}, {{C|FTL}}, and {{C|Overclock}}. * If not yet {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} by playing them, {{C|Boot Sequence}}, {{C|Chill}}, {{C|Fission}}, {{C|Reboot}}, and {{C|Seek}}. * If upgraded, {{C|Dualcast}}, {{C|Zap}}, and {{C|Recycle}}. * If upgraded and not yet {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} by playing them, {{C|Double Energy}} and {{C|White Noise}} * {{C|Streamline}} and {{C|Force Field}}, as long as they have been reduced to 0 cost already. === Neutral === * Cards with no concrete {{Icon|BE}}-cost, such as {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Statuses}}, and X-cost cards will never be put in hand by {{C|All for One}}. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 37: Darkness''' ** Scrape and All For One cards now correctly work with cards that set cost to 0 until played. * '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World''' ** This week adds the long anticipated third character into the game! ** A new character with unique mechanics, keywords, and art. ** Content: 75 Cards. {{DefectNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

If there are no other cards in hand when this card is played, no card will be [[Keywords#Discard|discarded]]. == Interactions == === Synergies === * Although the random targeting makes this unreliable, {{C|All-Out Attack}}'s [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] effect synergises with several [[Silent]] cards and relics: ==== Cards ==== * [[Keywords#Discard|Discarding]] {{C|Tactician}} or {{C|Reflex}} will immediately activate their effects. * {{C|Eviscerate}} is discounted by 1 {{Icon|GE}} Energy this turn. * {{C|Sneaky Strike}} will now refund 2 {{Icon|GE}} Energy if also played this turn. ==== Relics ==== * {{R|Tough Bandages}} will grant 3 {{KW|Block}}. * {{R|Tingsha}} will deal 3 damage to a random enemy. * {{R|Hovering Kite}} will generate 1 {{Icon|GE}} Energy if this is the first time a card has been [[Keywords#Discard|discarded]] this turn. === Neutral === * {{C|All-Out Attack}} can also be used to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] cards with end-of-turn effects, like {{C|Burn}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}} such as {{C|Regret}}. == Trivia == * The card's artwork, a cloud with fists popping out suggesting rapid beatings, is a reference to the move of the same name from the Persona series. == Update History == * '''Patch V1.1: The Dealer''' ** All-Out Attack, Madness, and Reboot cards no longer affect Card Rewards when used (rng issue). * '''Weekly Patch 45: Impatience''' ** All Out Attack card's discards now utilize seeds. * '''Weekly Patch 17: Patched in the Face''' ** All Out Attack card rework + buff. It adds a {{C|Beta}} into your draw pile, which in turn adds a {{C|Omega}} to your draw pile, which in turn gives you 50 (60 if {{C|Omega}} was upgraded)) {{BD|Omega}}. {{BD|Omega}} deals damage equal to its amount to '''ALL''' enemies at the end of your turn, every turn. When upgraded, {{C|Alpha}} becomes {{KW|Innate}}, meaning it will always appear in your first hand of combat. == Interactions == === Synergies === * As {{C|Beta}} and {{C|Omega}} can only be obtained in combat, they cannot be upgraded except within the combat itself. A previously played {{C|Master Reality}} will upgrade them upon being created, while {{C|Apotheosis}} or {{C|Armaments}} can upgrade them if they are respectively in your deck or hand. * Anything that allows you to dig through your draw pile synergizes well with this set of cards. ** {{KW|Scry}} lets you get to the next card in the set quicker. ** {{C|Omniscience}} allows you to immediately play any of the cards in the set, no matter where in your draw pile they are. ** Cards that allow you to place cards in your hand, such as {{C|Secret Technique}} and {{C|Seek}} are also extremely helpful. {{Clear}} == Beta == {{Card Infobox | Name = Beta | Link = Alpha#Beta | Image = Colorless-Beta.png | Color = Colorless | Type = Skill | Rarity = Special | Cost = 2 | CostPlus = 1 | Description = Shuffle an {{C|Omega}} into draw pile.

It adds an {{C|Omega}} to your draw pile, which in turn gives you 50 (60 if {{C|Omega}} was upgraded)) {{BD|Omega}}. {{BD|Omega}} deals damage equal to its amount to '''ALL''' enemies at the end of your turn, every turn. {{Clear}} == Omega == {{Card Infobox | Name = Omega | Link = Alpha#Omega | Image = Colorless-Omega.png | Color = Colorless | Type = Power | Rarity = Special | Cost = 3 | Description = At the end of your turn, deal (50;60) damage to ALL enemies. | GivesToPlayer = Omega }} {{Power Infobox | Name = Omega | Image = Icon Omega.png | Description = At the end of your turn, deal X damage to ALL enemies. | Type = Buff | Stacks = Intensity | BetweenTurns = Permanent | Cap = }} {{C|Omega}} is a 3 {{Icon|PE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colourless}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Special|Special}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives 50 (60 when upgraded) {{BD|Omega}}, which deals that much damage to all enemies at the end of each turn. === Interactions === ==== Order ==== {{BD|Omega}} activates before the enemy turn. On top of happening before enemy intents, it will also activate before: * Before {{BD|Invincible}} resets * Before {{BD|Poison}} activates When alongside other [[Buffs]] or [[Debuffs]] which activate at the end of the player's turn, {{BD|Omega}} activates in the order the buffs were gained. This includes: * {{BD|The Bomb}} * {{BD|Regen}} * {{BD|Constricted}} * {{BD|Combust}} Other notable interactions: * {{BD|Blasphemer}} kills the player at the start their turn, so the player will activate {{BD|Omega}} one more time before receiving damage ==== Synergies ==== * As {{C|Omega}} can only be obtained in combat, it cannot be upgraded except within the combat itself. A previously played {{C|Master Reality}} will upgrade it upon being created, while {{C|Apotheosis}} or {{C|Armaments}} can upgrade it if it is respectively in your deck or hand. ==== Neutral ==== * This damage is not affected by {{BD|Vulnerable}}, {{BD|Strength}}, or {{BD|Double Damage}}. == Trivia == * {{C|Omega}} is one of only 3 {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Common|Common}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} in the game, the other two being {{C|Become Almighty}} and {{C|Live Forever}}. All of these cards are obtained from playing {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Purple|Watcher}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skills}}. However, {{C|Omega}} is the only one that can be held in hand. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 13|* Fixed Omega power vfx appearing on dead enemies.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 11|* Adding a VFX for Omega power when it deals damage.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 7|* Beta+ card now costs 1 and generates Omega (not Omega+)}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 6|* Beta card gets buffed. Now shuffles Omega into the draw pile, rather than bottom of draw pile.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 4|* Omega card buff. Now deals its damage at end of turn.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 2|* Beta, Omega, and other new cards now appear in the Card Library.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 1|* Added Alpha, Beta, and Omega to the game ''(likely)''}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{WatcherNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

{{C|Amplify}} is a 1 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) {{BD|Amplify}}, which will make the following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card(s) this turn play twice, for the first amount of cards equal to the amount of {{BD|Amplify}}. 

Having more than 1 {{BD|Amplify}} will not increase the amount of times a single {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card is duplicated, but increases the amount of cards that can be duplicated when played.

The second play of these cards does not expend any {{Icon|BE}} '''Energy'''.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card only starts after the first play is fully resolved. In effect, it is as if the two cards were played with a pause in between, resulting in interactions including but not limited to:
** The first play of {{C|Heatsinks}} or {{C|Storm}} will already be activated by the second play.
** The first play of {{C|After Image}} will already give {{KW|Block}} because of the second play.

=== Neutral ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card counts as the play of a wholly separate card. All consequences of playing that card will still apply:
** The effects of the card itself.
** Anything that triggers or increments upon playing a ({{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}) card, including but not limited to: 
*** Effects such as {{BD|Storm}} or {{BD|Heatsink}}.
*** Relics such as {{R|Bird-Faced Urn}} and {{R|Ink Bottle}}.
*** Card limits such as {{R|Velvet Choker}} and the Time Eater's {{BD|Time Warp}}.  

== Trivia ==
* Along with {{C|Double Tap}} and {{C|Burst}}, one of the three 'play a card twice' Skills in the game.
* In [[Slay the Spire 2:Main|Slay the Spire 2]], this card was redesigned into {{C2|Signal Boost}}.
* This card's [[Beta Art]] shows the [[Defect]], [[Ironclad]], and [[Silent]] having a nice party. The [[Watcher]] was not invited.
** She was not in the game at this time.
** This card's [[Beta Art]] is likely a reference to the film ''Say Anything...''

It {{KW|Upgrade|upgrades}} every card in the player's hand, draw pile, discard pile, and exhaust pile. == Obtaining Apotheosis == {{C|Apotheosis}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card, and therefore can be obtained in the following ways: * Can be bought from the [[Merchant]]. * Can appear in the {{E|Sensory Stone}} event, from a choice of 3-9 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards, depending on the option that is selected. * Can be obtained from [[Monsters]], [[Elites]] and [[Bosses]] with {{R|Prismatic Shard}}. ** Also found in the [[Custom Mode|Daily Climb]] with the {{KW|Diverse}} or {{KW|Colorless Cards}} modifiers. * Can be obtained from Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a negative effect. == Interactions == === Order === * Cards that are created ''after'' {{C|Apotheosis}} has already been played (such as the {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} created by {{C|Blade Dance}}, the random cards created by {{R|Dead Branch}}, or cards generated by {{P|Attack Potion}}, {{P|Skill Potion}}, or {{P|Power Potion}}) will not be {{KW|Upgrade|upgraded}}. * Since {{C|Apotheosis}} {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausts}}, playing it while having {{R|Dead Branch}} will add a random card to the player's hand. However, {{C|Apotheosis}} will trigger its effect before {{R|Dead Branch}} creates the card, so it will not be {{KW|Upgrade|upgraded}}. * {{C|Apotheosis}} does not {{KW|Upgrade|upgrade}} itself. === Synergies === * Using {{R|Bottled Lightning}} to put {{C|Apotheosis}} in the player's starting hand can allow them to immediately {{KW|Upgrade|upgrade}} all their cards at the start of combat. * {{C|Master Reality}} can be used to {{KW|Upgrade|upgrade}} cards that are created after {{C|Apotheosis}} is played, since its effect only {{KW|Upgrade|upgrades}} the cards that the player currently has in their hand, draw pile, discard pile, and exhaust pile. === Neutral === * {{C|Armaments}} may only be able to {{KW|Upgrade|upgrade}} cards before {{C|Apotheosis}} is played. ** If the player has cards or other effects that generate cards in the middle of combat, then {{C|Armaments}} will be able to {{KW|Upgrade|upgrade}} them as normal since they will not have been {{KW|Upgrade|upgraded}} by {{C|Apotheosis}}. == Trivia == * "Apotheosis" is the act of becoming divine or god-likehttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apotheosis. * The card art for Apotheosis is reminiscent of the art for the Priest talent of the same name in Blizzard Entertainment's ''World of Warcraft''https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Apotheosis and may have been the inspiration for its art in Slay the Spire. ** The same art from World of Warcraft was re-used for the Hearthstone card of the same namehttps://hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Apotheosis, also developed by Blizzard Entertainment and set in the Warcraft universe. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 44|* The word "all" is all-caps in certain scenarios. title: Ascender's Bane
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox | Name = Ascender's Bane | Image = Curse-AscendersBane.png | Color = Colorless | Type = Curse | Cost = -2 | NoUpgrade = true | Description = {{KW|Unplayable}}.
{{KW|Ethereal}}.
Cannot be removed from your deck. | GivesToPlayer = Unplayable, Ethereal }} {{Keyword Infobox|Unplayable}} {{Keyword Infobox|Ethereal}} {{C|Ascender's Bane}} is an {{KW|Unplayable}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} Card. It is {{KW|Ethereal}}, and cannot be '''removed''' from your deck or {{KW|Transform|Transformed}} by any means. == Obtaining Ascender's Bane == On {{Asc|10|Ascension 10}} and higher, runs begin with a copy of '''Ascender's Bane''' in your starting deck. As there is no way to remove the card, high Ascension runs must always contend with at least one {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} in the deck. As there is no other way to obtain a copy, '''Ascender's Bane''' is the only piece of game content locked behind [[Ascension]]. == Interactions == === Order === {{KW|Ethereal}} causes '''Ascender's Bane''' to {{KW|Exhaust}} after your hand is discarded for the turn. If this causes you to draw from {{C|Dark Embrace}} or gain a card from {{R|Dead Branch}}, those cards will remain in your hand until your next turn. === Synergies === As '''Ascender's Bane''' is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal '''6(10)''' damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you '''+1''' {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. ** However, as '''Ascender's Bane''' generally '''Exhausts''' at end of turn anyway, this is only helpful in unusual circumstances. For instance, losing the '''HP''' can trigger {{R|Centennial Puzzle}} at will. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you '''6 max HP''' if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. However, since you start the game with your original copy, the only way for this to happen is if you duplicate the original. As Ascender's Bane is {{KW|Ethereal}}, it interacts with the following: * When it '''Exhausts''', {{C|Feel No Pain}} gains you {{KW|Block}}. * Similarly, {{C|Dark Embrace}} will draw you cards, and {{R|Dead Branch}} will generate a card to replace it. These cards will be kept in your hand until your next turn. * {{R|Charon's Ashes}} will deal damage to all enemies. * {{R|Strange Spoon}} only affects cards that {{KW|Exhaust}} when played, so it will never prevent '''Ascender's Bane''' from '''Exhausting''' (unless you are doing so with {{R|Blue Candle}}). === Neutral === * Being {{KW|Ethereal}}, Ascender's Bane will {{KW|Exhaust}} if it is in your hand at end of turn, even if it is {{KW|Retain|Retained}}. === Anti-Synergies === * If '''Ascender's Bane''' is discarded, you may end up drawing it again. This is sometimes the correct thing to do, but it does introduce a downside to {{C|Calculated Gamble}}, {{C|Storm of Steel}}, and {{C|Unload}}, which will all force you to discard it. ** {{C|All-Out Attack}} may also sometimes discard it unnecessarily. * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as '''Ascender's Bane''', it cannot be played. == Trivia == Despite '''Ascender's Bane''''s in game text only saying it cannot be '''removed''', it also can't be '''Transformed'''. However it can be '''duplicated''' using {{E|Duplicator}} and {{R|Dolly's Mirror}}. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 21|* Ascender's Bane was using the wrong apostrophe, causing data upload issues.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 18|* Ascender's Bane nerf: now has Ethereal. * Neow can no longer remove Ascender's Bane.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 17|* Ascender's Bane: Replaces Parasite for Ascension 10. * Ascender's Bane can no longer be removed by Back to Basics event. * Ascender's Bane can no longer be removed through the Wheel event. * Ascender's Bane gets marked as seen when you obtain it now. * Curse Card - Ascender's Bane: Unplayable. Cannot be removed from your deck. * Ascension 10 now gives you Ascender's Bane rather than Parasite.}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

== Interactions ==
=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{KW|Block}} carried over from the previous turn through {{R|Calipers}} will cause this card to have no effect.

* Any {{KW|Block}} gained before playing {{C|Auto-Shields}} will cause it to have no effect, unless the {{KW|Block}} gained is removed in the meantime, such as through {{BD|Thorns}} or {{BD|Beat of Death}}. This means that:
** {{C|Auto-Shields}} does not synergize with itself. In the same way, playing it multiple times with {{C|Echo Form}} or a {{P|Duplication Potion}} gives the same amount of {{KW|Block}} as simply playing it once.
** Using {{C|Hologram}} to place {{C|Auto-Shields}} back in hand will cause {{C|Auto-Shields}} to have no effect.
** Any activation of {{KW|Frost|Frost Orbs}} before playing {{C|Auto-Shields}} will cause it to have no effect. {{BD|Loop}} or {{R|Emotion Chip}} can trigger the passive ability of a {{KW|Frost|Frost Orb}} at the start of your turn, while {{C|Coolheaded}} or {{C|Fission|upgraded Fission}} can {{KW|Evoke}} {{KW|Frost|Frost Orbs}} while drawing {{C|Auto-Shields}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
==== General Orb Synergies ====
* Other Orb sources, such as {{C|Darkness}} and {{C|Coolheaded}}, can be very helpful for {{KW|Evoke|Evoking}} {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} more frequently.
* {{C|Thunder Strike}} hits more times for each {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orb}} {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} this combat, and {{C|Electrodynamics}} makes {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} hit all enemies.
* Sources of {{BD|Focus}} will improve the effects of Orbs: {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Consume}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, {{R|Data Disk}}
* Sources of additional Orb Slots allow for having more [[Orbs#Passive|Orb Passives]] in parallel: {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, {{P|Potion of Capacity}}
* {{C|Bullseye}} applies {{BD|Lock-On}}, which makes damaging Orbs deal 50% more damage to that enemy.
* {{C|Compile Driver}} draws a card for each unique type of Orb {{KW|Channel|Channeled}}.
* {{C|Barrage}} deals damage for each {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} Orb, while {{C|Fission}} draws a card and adds 1 {{Icon|BE}} for each Channeled Orb.
* {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}} each can directly {{KW|Evoke}} your Orbs 1, 2, or X times respectively.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, making {{KW|Lightning}} Orbs less effective.

title: Biased Cognition
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox |Name = Biased Cognition |Image = Blue-BiasedCognition.png |Color = Blue |Type = Power |Rarity = Rare |Cost = 1 |Description = Gain (4;5) {{BD|Focus}}.
At the start of your turn, lose 1 {{BD|Focus}}. |GivesToPlayer = Bias, Focus }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Bias |Image = Icon Bias.png |Description = At the start of your turn, lose X {{BD|Focus}}. |Type = Debuff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = Integer limit |GivesToPlayer = Focus (Negative) }} {{C|Biased Cognition}} is a 1 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}. == Interactions == === Order === * {{BD|Bias}} removes {{BD|Focus}} ''after'' the additional [[Orbs#Passive|Passives]] from {{C|Loop}} and {{R|Emotion Chip}} happen, despite the numbers on the Orbs changing visually first. * If an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} and a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} have already been played this turn, playing Biased Cognition may trigger {{R|Orange Pellets}}. If it does, {{BD|Bias}} will be cleared immediately. * In general, additive effects are applied before multiplicative ones. If a damaging Orb is improved by {{BD|Focus}} and then damages an enemy with {{BD|Lock-On}}, the {{BD|Focus}} will be added before the 50% increase from {{BD|Lock-On}}. === Synergies === * Like all sources of {{BD|Focus}}, Biased Cognition improves the output of {{KW|Lightning}}, {{KW|Frost}}, and {{KW|Dark}} Orbs. * Sources of {{BD|Focus}} stack, so Biased Cognition also works well with {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Consume}}, and {{R|Data Disk}}. * {{BD|Bias}} is a [[Debuff]], and can be prevented with sources of {{BD|Artifact}} such as {{C|Core Surge}}, as well as removed by {{R|Orange Pellets}}. ** Note that the {{BD|Artifact}} has to be applied ''before'' Biased Cognition is played. Otherwise, the {{BD|Artifact}} will only consume the first removal of {{BD|Focus}}, if anything. ** On the other hand, {{R|Orange Pellets}} has to happen ''after'' the {{BD|Bias}} is applied, but this can be triggered by playing Biased Cognition itself. If {{R|Orange Pellets}} is activated on a subsequent turn, {{BD|Bias}} will still be cleared, but any {{BD|Focus}} lost in the interrim is not restored (unless you have negative {{BD|Focus}}). * {{C|Bullseye}} applies {{BD|Lock-On}}, which makes damaging Orbs deal 50% more damage to that enemy, and applies after {{BD|Focus}} for large damage output. === Neutral === * Stacking {{BD|Bias}} will result in losing multiple {{BD|Focus}} per turn. * {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} are wholly unaffected by {{BD|Focus}}. * At first glance, it appears Biased Cognition will break even after 4 (5) turns. However, the value gained from {{BD|Focus}} in the meantime makes it take longer than that. Consider a simple example where you only have a single {{KW|Lightning}} Orb. If you play Biased Cogntition, it will deal 7 damage, then 6, then 5, etc. After 7 turns, you will have dealt 28 damage with Biased Cognition, and your {{BD|Focus}} will now be 0. On the other hand, if you hadn't played it, you'd deal 3 damage every turn, for a total of just 21 damage after 7 turns, and would still require another 3 turns to surpass the former example. === Anti-Synergies === * {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, undoing the benefit of Biased Cognition. However, as Biased Cognition will eventually remove all of its own {{BD|Focus}} anyway, {{C|Hyperbeam}} can still be useful as a finisher. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World''' ** This week adds the long anticipated third character into the game! ** A new character with unique mechanics, keywords, and art. ** Content: 75 Cards. {{DefectNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

When played, the card exhausts and causes Watcher to enter {{KW|Divinity|Divinity}}, which grants 3 {{Icon|PE}} Energy and triples the damage of your attacks for the rest of the turn. The price of this effect is that the Watcher becomes a {{BD|Blasphemer}}, ensuring 99999 self damage next turn. When upgraded, the card {{KW|Retain|Retains}}. == Interactions == === Synergies === * {{KW|Retain|Retaining}} attacks in hand such as {{C|Windmill Strike}} ensures you will have ammo for when {{C|Blasphemy}} is used. * {{BD|Vulnerable}} scales multiplicatively with {{KW|Divinity}} for a massive total 4.5x damage multiplier. * {{C|Blasphemy}} generates a lot of energy, which greatly benefits from card draw. * {{R|Lizard Tail}} and {{P|Fairy in a Bottle}} allows you to survive {{BD|Blasphemer}}. * As the upgraded version of {{C|Blasphemy}} {{KW|Retain|Retains}}, {{C|Establishment}} will decrease it in {{Icon|PE}}-cost at the end of a turn, unless it already costs 0. ==== Negating Blasphemer ==== Despite the card text of {{C|Blasphemy}} outright telling that it kills Watcher, it actually deals 99999 HP loss, which can be prevented. * {{R|Fossilized Helix}} completely blocks {{BD|Blasphemer}}. * {{BD|Intangible}} reduces {{BD|Blasphemer}} damage to 1. However, since {{BD|Intangible}} counts down at the beginning of your turn, you need at least 2 stacks to protect yourself. ** {{R|Incense Burner}} gives {{BD|Intangible}} at the beginning of your turn, so it can protect you even though it grants only 1 stack. Make sure its counter is on 5 the turn you play {{C|Blasphemy}}. ** Since {{BD|Blasphemer}} is HP loss, the 1 cannot be blocked by regular {{KW|Block}} cards. === Neutral === * {{C|Blasphemy}} does not generate {{BD|Mantra}}, so it does not scale up the damage of {{C|Brilliance}}. === Anti-Synergies === * {{BD|Blasphemer}} is intentionally treated as a "[[Buffs|positive buff]]" by the game, and thus cannot be blocked by {{BD|Artifact}} or removed with {{R|Orange Pellets}}. * Cards that change your {{KW|Stance}} will remove {{KW|Divinity}} without removing the {{BD|Blasphemer}} effect. * {{C|Conclude}}, {{C|Meditate}}, {{C|Vault}} and {{BD|Time Warp}} forcibly end your turn, likely resulting in your death. * Effects that play cards from your draw pile for free (like {{C|Mayhem}} and {{P|Distilled Chaos}}) may end up playing {{C|Blasphemy}} before you are ready. * {{BD|Invincible}} and {{BD|Unawakened}} may prevent you from ending the combat in one turn. == Trivia == * Max HP is not capped in Slay the Spire, which means it's possible (but unfeasible) to increase your HP so high you can survive {{BD|Blasphemer}}. ** One way this could be done is using 2 {{C|Nightmare|Nightmares}} to generate a large number of {{C|Nightmare|Nightmares}}, then using these cards to {{C|Wish}} for a massive quantity of [[Gold]], which can be used with {{R|The Courier}} to buy an endless amount of {{P|Fruit Juice}} at the [[Merchant]]. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 10|* Adding polished card portrait for Blasphemy.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 7|* Blasphemy+ card now gives Retain on upgrade, cost remains at 1.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 5|* Blasphemy card now exhausts when played.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 2|* Tungesten Rod no longer stops Blasphemy from killing you. * Lightning strikes down the Blasphemer.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 1|* Added XXX to the game {{C|Bouncing Flask}} is a 2 {{Icon|GE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy's turn, it has some unusual interactions:
* If the damage is enough to cause {{M|The Guardian}} to change to Defensive form, it will immediately change its [[Intent]] to apply {{BD|Sharp Hide}}. Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn.
** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected.
* If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn.
** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn.
* If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn.
* If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking.

=== Synergies ===
* {{C|Bane}} does additional damage if the target has {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Catalyst}} can double (triple) the amount of {{BD|Poison}} on a target.
* {{R|The Specimen}} can be used in combats with multiple enemies to consolidate {{BD|Poison}} as enemies die.
* {{R|Snecko Skull}} applies 1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever this card applies {{BD|Poison}}, meaning it activates 3 (4 if this card is upgraded) times.

* {{C|Bouncing Flask}} works well with other sources of {{BD|Poison}}:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Deadly Poison}}, {{C|Poisoned Stab}}, {{C|Crippling Cloud}}, {{C|Noxious Fumes}}, {{C|Corpse Explosion}}, {{C|Envenom}}.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Twisted Funnel}}.
* {{P|Poison Potion}}.

=== Neutral ===
* {{BD|Poison}} bypasses {{KW|Block}} and {{BD|Flying}}.
* {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process.
* However, {{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{BD|Artifact}} will prevent applying {{BD|Poison}}.
** However, as Bouncing Flask applies Poison multiple times in a single card play, it can be very effective at clearing {{BD|Artifact}} for your other {{BD|Poison}} cards.
* Certain bosses will remove all [[Debuffs]] during combat: {{M|The Champ}}, {{M|Awakened One}}, and {{M|Time Eater}}.

== Update History ==
* '''Weekly Patch 54: Loop'''
** Tingsha, Sword Boomerang, Bouncing Flask, Rip and Tear, Thunder Orbs, Havoc, and Juggernaut now utilize seeded enemy target randomization.

* '''Weekly Patch 10: Quality of Life'''
** Bouncing Flask no longer loses bounces to dead enemies.

* '''Day 1 Patch'''
Adding null check for Bouncing Flask VFX to prevent odd crashes.

|BetweenTurns = 
|Cap          =

{{C|Burst}} is a 1 {{Icon|GE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) {{BD|Burst}}, which will make the following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card(s) this turn play twice, for the first amount of cards equal to the amount of {{BD|Burst}}. 

Having more than 1 {{BD|Burst}} will not increase the amount of times a single {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card is duplicated, but increases the amount of cards that can be duplicated when played.

The second play of these cards counts as a separate card being played, but this card is not added to your draw or discard pile, and is not {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} unless the card would {{KW|Exhaust}} upon being played normally. 

The second play of these cards does not expend any {{Icon|GE}} '''Energy'''. The second play of an X-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card will use the same value of X as the first.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card only starts after the first play is fully resolved. In effect, it is as if the two cards were played with a pause in between, resulting in interactions including but not limited to:
** The second play of {{C|Catalyst}} will multiply the {{BD|Poison}} that was already multiplied by the first play, effectively squaring the effect of the card.
** The second play of {{C|Calculated Gamble}} or {{C|Storm of Steel}} will [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] the cards that were respectively drawn or generated by the first play.

=== Synergies ===
* As {{C|Burst}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}}, it can duplicate itself, resulting in more {{BD|Burst}}, which means more {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skills}} being duplicated.
** For example, if the player has no {{BD|Burst}} and plays {{C|Burst}}, {{C|Burst}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}} and {{C|Catalyst}}, in that order, the order of operations will be:
# The first {{C|Burst}} provides the player with the {{BD|Burst}} effect. 
# The second {{C|Burst}} is now played twice, consuming the initial {{BD|Burst}} but then providing 2 additional stacks of it. 
# {{C|Bouncing Flask}} is then played twice and one {{BD|Burst}} will be consumed.
# {{C|Catalyst}} is then played twice and the last {{BD|Burst}} will be consumed.

=== Neutral ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card counts as the play of a wholly separate card. All consequences of playing that card will still apply:
** The effects of the card itself.
** Anything that triggers or increments upon playing a ({{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}}) card, including but not limited to: 
*** Effects such as {{BD|After Image}} and {{BD|Thousand Cuts}}.
*** Relics such as {{R|Letter Opener}} and {{R|Ink Bottle}}.
*** Card limits such as {{R|Velvet Choker}} and the Time Eater's {{BD|Time Warp}}.

* Using {{BD|Burst}} on {{C|Blade Dance}} creates 6 (8 if {{C|Blade Dance}} is upgraded) {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} in hand, which can significantly advance counters on relics such as {{R|Shuriken}} and {{R|Nunchaku}} when played, but potentially exceeds the hand size limit in which case the remaining {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} will be added to the discard pile.

=== Anti-Synergies === 
* Since {{C|Panic Button}} immediately applies the {{BD|No Block}} debuff, using {{BD|Burst}} on {{C|Panic Button}} provides no extra {{KW|Block}}. 
* Since the first play of {{C|Expertise}} will fill the hand to the specified amount of cards, the second play will have no effect.

== Bugs ==
=== Bursting a Burst ===
On the Mobile version, there is a bug that can occur when Bursting a Burst. If you have exactly 1 stack of Burst, and you play Burst, then what happens is:
* The first play of Burst will occur, adding 1 (2) stacks.
* The game attempts to remove the stack of Burst that has been consumed. Due to a bug, it then removes '''all stacks of Burst, including the one(s) just added'''.
* The second play will happen, adding 1 (2) stacks.
Instead of ending up with 2 (4) stacks afterwards as expected, you will only have 1 (2), the same as if you hadn't Burst it at all.

If you have 2 or more stacks of Burst and play Burst, the game handles the interaction properly.

== Trivia ==

* Along with {{C|Double Tap}} and {{C|Amplify}}, one of the three 'play a card twice' Skills in the game.

If this causes you to draw from {{C|Dark Embrace}} or gain a card from {{R|Dead Branch}}, those cards will remain in your hand until your next turn. === Synergies === As Clumsy is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. ** However, as Clumsy generally Exhausts at end of turn anyway, this is only helpful in unusual circumstances. For instance, losing the HP can trigger {{R|Centennial Puzzle}} at will. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. {{C|Creative AI}} is a 3 (2 if upgraded) {{Icon|BE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives you one {{BD|Creative AI}}, which adds 1 {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card into your hand at the start of each turn. 

{{BD|Creative AI}} can only generate {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} cards you can find in card rewards through character choice or custom run modifiers, and is not affected by {{R|Prismatic Shard}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{BD|Creative AI}} takes effect before your cards are drawn. This means that having a high amount of {{BD|Creative AI}} can cause you to draw less cards at the start of your turn due to the hand size limit.

=== Synergies ===
* Synergizes with {{C|Storm}} and {{C|Heatsinks}} which get activated every time a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card is played. Both of these cards can also be generated by {{BD|Creative AI}}.
* Synergizes with {{C|Force Field}}, as it ensures enough {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} will be available to eventually lower the cost of {{C|Force Field}} to 0, and already discounts it by 1 {{Icon|BE}} '''Energy''' itself.
* Synergizes extremely well with power-dependent relics, as {{R|Mummified Hand}} makes it easier to play all generated {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} cards, and {{R|Bird-Faced Urn}} allows you to heal to full HP if combat lasts long enough.

=== Neutral ===
* If a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card generated by this card exceeds your hand size limit, it gets added to the discard pile.
* Some {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} cards cannot be generated, as they have some permanent effect out of combat, or can only be obtained from another source.

=== Excluded Cards ===
As with most random card generation effects, {{C|Creative AI}} cannot generate cards that are unobtainable from card rewards or cards that can heal the player. The following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} will never be generated by {{C|Creative AI}}:
* {{C|Self Repair}} (healing)
* {{C|Omega}} (can only be generated during combat via {{C|Alpha}} and {{C|Beta}})
* All {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless&type:Power|Colorless powers}} ({{C|Creative AI}} will only generate {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} of the player character's color and is not affected by {{R|Prismatic Shard}})

{{Power Infobox|Poison}}{{C|Deadly Poison}} is a 1 {{Icon|GE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Common|Common}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy's turn, it has some unusual interactions:
* If the damage is enough to cause {{M|The Guardian}} to change to Defensive form, it will immediately change its [[Intent]] to apply {{BD|Sharp Hide}}. Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn.
** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected.
* If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn.
** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn.
* If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn.
* If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking.

=== Synergies ===
* {{C|Bane}} does additional damage if the target has {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Catalyst}} can double (triple) the amount of {{BD|Poison}} on a target.
* {{R|The Specimen}} can be used in combats with multiple enemies to consolidate {{BD|Poison}} as enemies die.
* {{R|Snecko Skull}} applies 1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever this card applies {{BD|Poison}}.

* {{C|Deadly Poison}} works well with other sources of {{BD|Poison}}:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Poisoned Stab}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}}, {{C|Crippling Cloud}}, {{C|Noxious Fumes}}, {{C|Corpse Explosion}}, {{C|Envenom}}.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Twisted Funnel}}.
* {{P|Poison Potion}}.

=== Neutral ===
* {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process.
* {{BD|Poison}} bypasses {{KW|Block}} and {{BD|Flying}}.
* However, {{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{BD|Artifact}} will prevent applying {{BD|Poison}}.
* Certain bosses will remove all [[Debuffs]] during combat: {{M|The Champ}}, {{M|Awakened One}}, and {{M|Time Eater}}.

== Update History ==
* '''Weekly Patch 18: Paranormal'''
** Deadly Poison card buff: 4 -> 5. Upgraded: 6 -> 7.

title: Decay
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox |Name = Decay |Image = Curse-Decay.png |Color = Colorless |Type = Curse |Cost = -2 |NoUpgrade = true |Description = {{KW|Unplayable}}.
At the end of your turn, take 2 damage. |GivesToPlayer = Unplayable }} {{Keyword Infobox|Unplayable}} {{C|Decay}} is an {{KW|Unplayable}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} Card. If it is in your hand at end of turn, it will [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] itself, and deal 2 damage to you. == Obtaining Decay == Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Decay can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse: * Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward. * {{E|Match and Keep}}. * {{R|Cursed Key}}. * {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse. In addition, Decay can be obtained from the {{E|Forgotten Altar}} and {{E|Wheel of Change}} [[Events]]. == Interactions == === Order === * Decay will discard itself at the end of your turn before the rest of your hand, at the same time it applies the damage. This happens ''before'' {{KW|Retain}} happens, so you cannot choose to Retain it. * Decay, {{C|Burn|Burns}}, {{C|Shame}}, {{C|Doubt}}, and {{C|Regret}} all activate at the same time at end of turn. Visually they activate from left to right. However: ** Regardless of the order of activation, {{C|Regret}} counts any copies of the others as being still in your hand when its damage is applied. ** If Decay, {{C|Regret}}, or {{C|Burn}} cause you to draw into any of the above via {{R|Runic Cube}}, those newly drawn cards will ''not'' go off, and will be discarded with the rest of your hand. ** The damage for Decay, {{C|Burn}}, and {{C|Regret}} are applied from left to right. So, if you have 1 stack of {{BD|Buffer}} and two of them in hand, the left one will have its damage consumed, and the right one will apply. *** When selecting cards from your hand, such as to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] or {{KW|Exhaust}}, you can freely reorder your hand, as selecting and then unselecting a card moves it to the last spot in your hand. If needed, this can be used to manipulate which card's damage is applied to you. === Synergies === As Decay is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. The damage dealt with Decay can be: * Negated with {{BD|Buffer}}, via {{R|Fossilized Helix}} and {{C|Buffer}}. * Reduced to 1 with {{BD|Intangible}}, via {{R|Incense Burner}}, {{C|Wraith Form}}, and {{C|Apparition}}. * Reduced by 1 with {{R|Tungsten Rod}}. However, as Decay only does 2 damage and can be blocked, these are generally not needed. The damage dealt by Decay can also be used to your benefit if it causes you to lose HP: * Losing HP causes {{R|Runic Cube}} to draw you a card. * {{C|Blood for Blood}} will have its cost reduced for the rest of combat. * The HP loss is counted as being from a card, so {{C|Rupture}} will gain you {{BD|Strength}}. === Neutral === * As Decay deals damage rather than causing HP loss directly, it can be prevented with {{KW|Block}}, unlike {{C|Regret}} and {{C|Pain}}. * Decay generally cannot be {{KW|Retain|Retained}}, and does not stay in your hand with {{R|Runic Pyramid}}, as it discards itself as part of its end of turn activation. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Decay, it cannot be played. * If the damage dealt by Decay causes you to lose HP, {{C|Masterful Stab}} will have its cost increased for the rest of combat. == Trivia == Decay can be seen as the Curse equivalent of the {{C|Burn}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Status}}. Both deal 2 damage to you at end of turn, and their end of turn interactions are identical. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly |* Fixed issue where Regret/Decay/Doubt/Burn fails to exhaust via Blue Candle and Medical Kit.}} {{Update History Table/row|?|* Added Decay to the game}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

It shuffles your discard pile into your draw pile, then draws 1 (2 if upgraded) cards. == Obtaining Deep Breath == {{C|Deep Breath}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card, and therefore can be obtained in the following ways: * Can be bought from the [[Merchant]]. * Can appear in the {{E|Sensory Stone}} event, from a choice of 3-9 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards, depending on the option that is selected. * Can be obtained from Neow's [[First Blessing]] via the {{TS|green||'''Obtain an Uncommon Colorless Card'''}} bonus. * Can be obtained from [[Monsters]] and [[Elites]] with {{R|Prismatic Shard}}. ** Also found in [[Custom Mode|Daily Climb]] with the {{KW|Diverse}} or {{KW|Colorless Cards}} modifiers. * Can be obtained from the {{Frame|Success?}} option at {{E|Knowing Skull}}. == Interactions == === Synergies === * Shuffling with this card counts for relics that depend on shuffling your deck, so {{R|The Abacus}} and {{R|Sundial}} will trigger more often as a result of using {{C|Deep Breath}}. * It maximizes the amount of cards in your draw pile, so it synergizes with {{C|Aggregate}} and {{C|Mind Blast}}, as well as any cards take effect on cards in your draw pile, such as {{C|Seek}}, {{C|Omniscience}}, or {{C|Violence}}. === Neutral === * If your discard pile is empty, your draw pile will not be shuffled. === Anti-Synergies === * It minimizes the amount of cards in your discard pile, so it negatively affects {{C|Stack}}, as well as any cards that take effect on cards in your discard pile, such as {{C|Headbutt}} and {{C|All for One}}. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 47|* Reboot and Deep Breath cards no longer trigger shuffle-based relics twice.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 8|* Colorless cards can now be upgraded! This was also a good time to re-examine and balance several of the cards. * Deep Breath+. == Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* In general, additive effects are applied before multiplicative ones. If a damaging Orb is improved by {{BD|Focus}} and then damages an enemy with {{BD|Lock-On}}, the {{BD|Focus}} will be added before the 50% increase from {{BD|Lock-On}}.

=== Synergies ===
* Like all sources of {{BD|Focus}}, Defragment improves the output of {{KW|Lightning}}, {{KW|Frost}}, and {{KW|Dark}} Orbs.
* Sources of {{BD|Focus}} stack, so Defragment also works well with {{C|Consume}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, and {{R|Data Disk}}.
* As increasing {{BD|Focus}} makes each of your non-{{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} better, sources of {{BD|Focus}} generally scale multiplicatively with sources of additional Orb Slots: {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, {{P|Potion of Capacity}}.
* {{C|Bullseye}} applies {{BD|Lock-On}}, which makes damaging Orbs deal 50% more damage to that enemy, and applies after {{BD|Focus}} for large damage output.

=== Neutral ===
* {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} are wholly unaffected by {{BD|Focus}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, undoing the benefit of Defragment.

{{C|Double Tap}} is a 1 {{Icon|RE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Red|Ironclad}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) stacks of {{BD|Double Tap}}, which will make the following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card(s) this turn play twice, for the first amount of cards equal to the amount of {{BD|Double Tap}}. 

Having more than 1 {{BD|Double Tap}} will not increase the amount of times a single {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card is duplicated, but increases the amount of cards that can be duplicated when played.

The second play of these cards counts as a separate card being played, but this card is not added to your draw or discard pile, and is not {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} unless the card would {{KW|Exhaust}} upon being played normally. 

The second play of these cards does not expend any {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy'''. The second play of an X-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card will use the same value of X as the first.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* The second play of an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card only starts after the first play is fully resolved. In effect, it is as if the two cards were played with a pause in between, resulting in interactions including but not limited to:
** The second play of {{C|Headbutt}} will be able to target the first play in the discard pile. 
** {{BD|Vigor}} will be consumed by the first play, and will not be used for the second play.
** {{BD|Strength}} gained by {{R|Shuriken}} by the first play will already affect the second play.
** {{BD|Malleable}} will already give the target {{KW|Block}} after the first play.

=== Neutral ===
* The second play of an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card counts as the play of a wholly separate card. All consequences of playing that card will still apply:
** The effects of the card itself.
** Anything that triggers or increments upon playing an ({{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}}) card, including but not limited to: 
*** Effects such as {{BD|Rage}}.
*** Relics such as {{R|Shuriken}} and {{R|Ink Bottle}}.
*** Card limits such as {{R|Velvet Choker}} and the Time Eater's {{BD|Time Warp}}.  

== Trivia ==

* Along with {{C|Burst}} and {{C|Amplify}}, one of the three 'play a card twice' Skills in the game.

== Update History ==
* '''Weekly Patch 46: Adrenaline'''
** Fix for proper behavior when duplicating cards like Rampage and Genetic Algorithm with effects like Echo Form.

* '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot'''
** Updating icon for Double Tap power.

* '''Weekly Patch 28: The Ritual'''
** Fixed issue where cards stayed after combat with Echo Form or Double Tap.

wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox | Name = Doubt | Image = Curse-Doubt.png | Color = Colorless | Type = Curse | Cost = -2 | NoUpgrade = true | Description = {{KW|Unplayable}}.
At the end of your turn, gain 1 {{BD|Weak}}. | GivesToPlayer = Weak, Unplayable }} {{Keyword Infobox|Unplayable}} {{Power Infobox|Weak}} {{C|Doubt}} is an {{KW|Unplayable}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} Card. If it is in your hand at end of turn, it will [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] itself, and apply 1 {{BD|Weak}} to you. == Obtaining Doubt == Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Doubt can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse: * Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward. * {{E|Match and Keep}}. * {{R|Cursed Key}}. * {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse. In addition, Doubt can be obtained from {{E|The Ssssserpent}} Event when choosing {{Frame|Agree}} as well as {{E|Mind Bloom}} when choosing {{Frame|I am Healthy}}. == Interactions == === Order === * Doubt will discard itself at the end of your turn before the rest of your hand, at the same time it applies the {{BD|Weak}}. This happens ''before'' {{KW|Retain}} happens, so you cannot choose to Retain it. * Doubt, {{C|Shame}}, {{C|Regret}}, {{C|Decay}}, and {{C|Burn|Burns}} all activate at the same time at end of turn. Visually they activate from left to right. However: ** Regardless of the order of activation, {{C|Regret}} counts any copies of the others as being still in your hand when its damage is applied. ** For Doubt and {{C|Shame}}, the [[Debuffs]] are applied from left to right. So, if you have 1 stack of {{BD|Artifact}} and both in hand, the left one will consume the Artifact and the right one will apply. *** When selecting cards from your hand, such as to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] or {{KW|Exhaust}}, you can freely reorder your hand, as selecting and then unselecting a card moves it to the last spot in your hand. If needed, this can be used to manipulate which Curse's debuff is applied to you. === Synergies === As Doubt is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. The {{BD|Weak}} debuff can be dealt with in a few ways: * It can be prevented with sources of {{BD|Artifact}}, such as {{C|Core Surge}} and {{C|Panacea}}. * It can be removed during your next turn with {{R|Orange Pellets}}. * The downside can be ignored by having a damage plan that doesn't require {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} cards, such as {{C|Juggernaut}}, {{C|A Thousand Cuts}}, {{BD|Poison}}, {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}}, {{KW|Dark|Dark Orbs}}, or {{C|The Bomb}}. * {{R|Runic Pyramid}} and {{KW|Retain}} effects such as {{C|Well-Laid Plans}} can allow you to save your key Attacks for when the {{BD|Weak}} has cleared. * {{C|Vault}} can be used to skip to your next turn, clearing the debuff without giving the enemy a turn. === Neutral === * Doubt cannot be {{KW|Retain|Retained}}, and does not stay in your hand with {{R|Runic Pyramid}}, as it discards itself as part of its end of turn activation. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Doubt, it cannot be played. == Trivia == * The beta design of Doubt is a reference to the Press X to Doubt meme. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly |* Fixed issue where Regret/Decay/Doubt/Burn fails to exhaust via Blue Candle and Medical Kit.}} {{Update History Table/row|?|* Added Doubt to the game}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

{{C|Dual Wield}} is a 1 {{Icon|RE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Red|Ironclad}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It allows you to select one {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card in your hand, and add 1 copy (2 copies if upgraded) of that card into your hand.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
* Duplicating any card with "Strike" in its name using {{C|Dual Wield}} will increase the damage of {{C|Perfected Strike}}, as it counts all cards in your deck during combat, not your actual deck.

=== Neutral ===
* When a card is copied, any changes to that card are also copied. The duration of these changes is initially the same for any copy as for the original. Once created, all copies behave fully independently.
** A changed energy cost is copied, through something like {{R|Snecko Eye}}, {{C|Madness}} or {{P|Liquid Memories}}, or through the automatic energy change of cards like {{C|Blood for Blood}} and {{C|Masterful Stab}}.
** Changes to the values of the card are copied, such as upgrades to {{C|Searing Blow}} or increased damage of {{C|Rampage}}.

* If a copy created by {{C|Dual Wield}} exceeds the hand size limit, it gets added to the discard pile.

== Bugs ==
* While playing {{C|Dual Wield}} on {{C|Ritual Dagger}}, if the '''"Choose a Card"''' prompt opens, the original {{C|Ritual Dagger}} copy is lost, meaning any scaling it does within this combat will not be carried over outside of combat.
** This can be prevented by making sure it is the only {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card in hand, and therefore not opening the prompt. In this case, the leftmost {{C|Ritual Dagger}} is the original copy.

* Under the effect of {{C|Master Reality}}, {{C|Dual Wield}} {{KW|Upgrade|Upgrades}} '''all''' cards, even the original card that was copied.

== Update History ==
* '''Weekly Update 40: Forethought'''
** Card copy effects like Dual Wield should now also copy the "free to play once" effect from cards like Setup and Forethought.

{{C|Envenom}} is a 2 (1) {{Icon|GE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* If {{C|Bane}} is played on an enemy with no {{BD|Poison}}, 1 will be added by the first hit of Bane, causing the second hit to occur.
* Although the {{BD|Poison}} applied by Envenom happens at the same time as the hit that caused it (i.e. before the next hit of the Attack), all triggers of {{C|Sadistic Nature}} will be applied after the attack finishes.

==== Poison Interactions ====
As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy's turn, it has some unusual interactions:
* If the damage is enough to cause {{M|The Guardian}} to change to Defensive form, it will immediately change its [[Intent]] to apply {{BD|Sharp Hide}}. Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn.
** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected.
* If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn.
** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn.
* If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn.
* If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking.

=== Synergies ===
* Attacks with multiple hits will trigger Envenom multiple times; for example, {{C|Riddle with Holes}}, {{C|Dagger Spray}}, and {{C|Skewer}}.
* {{C|Bane}} does additional damage if the target has {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Catalyst}} can double (triple) the amount of {{BD|Poison}} on a target.
* {{R|The Specimen}} can be used in combats with multiple enemies to consolidate {{BD|Poison}} as enemies die.
* {{R|Snecko Skull}} applies 1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever this card applies {{BD|Poison}}. It applies to each instance of {{BD|Poison}} separately. For instance, if you have Envenom and Snecko Skull, and hit an enemy with {{C|Glass Knife}}, that enemy will get 4 {{BD|Poison}}, not 3.

* {{C|Envenom}} works well with other sources of {{BD|Poison}}:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Deadly Poison}}, {{C|Poisoned Stab}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}}, {{C|Crippling Cloud}}, {{C|Noxious Fumes}}, {{C|Corpse Explosion}}.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Twisted Funnel}}.
* {{P|Poison Potion}}.

=== Neutral ===
* The Attack does have to actually deal damage. If the {{M|Corrupt Heart}}'s {{BD|Invincible}} cap is maxed out for the turn, additional Attacks will not apply any {{BD|Poison}} to it.
* {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process.
* {{BD|Poison}} bypasses {{KW|Block}} and {{BD|Flying}}.
* However, {{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{BD|Artifact}} will prevent applying {{BD|Poison}}.
** However, certain Attacks allow Envenom to deal several [[Debuffs]] in a single card play, clearing {{BD|Artifact}} for your other {{BD|Poison}} sources.
* Certain bosses will remove all [[Debuffs]] during combat: {{M|The Champ}}, {{M|Awakened One}}, and {{M|Time Eater}}.

== Update History ==

** Envenom's Poison is now applied immediately after the damage occurs.

** Updating icon for Envenom power.

* '''Weekly Patch 5: Happy Holidays!'''
** Envenom card gets a wording update for clarity.
** Updating description for Envenom power to mention unblocked dmg.

== Obtaining Eruption ==
The [[Watcher]] starts the game with one copy of {{C|Eruption}} in her deck. It cannot be obtained through regular card rewards, but can be obtained in the {{E|Match and Keep}} Event. 

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{C|Eruption}} first deals damage and only then makes you enter {{KW|Wrath}}, meaning its own damage is not yet doubled if you were not already in {{KW|Wrath}}. 

=== Synergies ===
* When entering {{KW|Wrath}} if you are not in {{KW|Wrath}} yet:
** If you have {{BD|Rushdown}} from {{C|Rushdown}}, you will draw that many cards.
** You will switch {{KW|Stance}}, which results in the following:
*** Any {{C|Flurry of Blows}} that was in your discard pile will be brought back to your hand, as long as there is space in hand.
*** {{C|Mental Fortress}} will give {{KW|Block}}.
*** If you were in the {{KW|Calm}} {{KW|Stance}} before, you will gain 2 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''', or 3 if you have {{R|Violet Lotus}}.

* Being in {{KW|Wrath}} changes the effects of some cards:
** {{C|Halt}} will give its additional {{KW|Block}}.
** {{C|Indignation}} will apply {{BD|Vulnerable}}.

=== Neutral ===
* While in {{KW|Wrath}}, all {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} damage you deal is doubled, but you also take double damage from enemy attacks.{{KW|Wrath}} only doubles damage from {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, not from effects such as {{BD|Panache}} or {{BD|Thorns}}, or relics such as {{R|Mercury Hourglass}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* As {{KW|Wrath}} is worse than the {{KW|Divinity}} {{KW|Stance}} in every way except for the aformentioned ones, using {{C|Eruption}} while in {{KW|Divinity}} is generally bad, if it does not end combat.

unupgraded version of {{C|Enlightenment}}. ** If {{C|Eviscerate}} already costed 0, {{C|Enlightenment}} will not increase it to 1. * {{C|Eviscerate}} copied by {{C|Dual Wield}} will cost the same as the original, while the copies made by {{C|Nightmare}} the next turn will not include the discounted energy cost achieved by anything other than {{C|Setup}}, {{C|Forethought}} or upgraded {{C|Enlightenment}} in the current turn. * When drawn with {{R|Snecko Eye}} or {{P|Snecko Oil}} the cost will always be randomised regardless of how many cards have previously been [[Keywords#Discard|discarded]]. === Anti-Synergies === * If '''Eviscerate''' is discounted through unupgraded {{C|Enlightenment}} or by [[Keywords#Discard|discarding]] cards, when it is fetched (example, with {{C|Secret Weapon}}), it will cost '''3'''. == Bugs == === Without Snecko Eye === ==== Infernal Blade ==== * If {{C|Eviscerate}} is generated from {{C|Infernal Blade}}, its cost will be determined by the number of [[Keywords#Discard|Discards]] this turn. It will NOT be generated at 0 {{Icon|GE}} unless 3 cards are Discarded. * For example, if 2 cards are [[Keywords#Discard|Discarded]] before {{C|Infernal Blade}} is played, the cost of {{C|Eviscerate}} will be 1 {{Icon|GE}}. ==== Fetched after Discard discount ==== * When fetched by {{C|Secret Weapon}}, {{C|Violence}}, {{C|Seek}}, {{C|Hologram}}, Eviscerate will always cost 3 {{Icon|GE}}, even if it was discounted by Discards. * {{C|All for One}} will not pull the 0 {{Icon|GE}} costed (from 3 Discarded cards) Eviscerate. * Does not apply to discounted by {{C|Setup}}, {{C|Forethought}}, and upgraded {{C|Enlightenment}}, these work like normal. ==== Soft discounts ==== These are discounts given by * {{C|Bullet Time}} * {{R|Mummified Hand}} * Unupgraded {{C|Enlightenment}} Or generated by * {{C|Foreign Influence}} * {{P|Attack Potion}} * {{C|Discovery}} ===== Duplicating after soft discount ===== If a soft discounted Eviscerate is duplicated by {{C|Echo Form}}, {{P|Duplication Potion}} or {{C|Double Tap}}, it will cost 3 {{Icon|GE}} instead of 0 {{Icon|GE}} '''on the second play.''' ===== Nightmare or Dual Wield after soft discount ===== If a soft discounted Eviscerate is played as a {{C|Nightmare}} target or {{C|Dual Wield}} target, it will return at 3 {{Icon|GE}} cost '''on the same turn'''. === With Snecko Eye === ==== Calculated Gamble ==== * Gambling into Eviscerate with Snecko Eye will make it cost 0 roughly 50%. * This is because the game has two types of cost: Permanent, and Temporary. When Eviscerate gets a discount through discards, the Temporary cost is changed. When Snecko Eye rolls for a cost and it matches the Permanent cost, it won't change Eviscerate's cost and Eviscerate will discount itself to 0 due to the Calculated Gamble. * Example: Eviscerate currently costs 3. When Calculated Gamble draws into it, it can cost 1 and 2 25% of the time. If the Snecko Eye cost rolls 3, it matches with Eviscerate's original cost and will discount itself to Calculated Gamble. ===== Nightmare after Calculated Gamble ===== * There is a chance that an Eviscerate that costs 0 after being Gambled into, when Nightmared, will not cost 0 next turn. * This is because Eviscerate will only retain the 0 cost if the cost was given by Snecko, and not if the cost was given by discards. There is no way to predict the cost of these copies. ==== Nightmare or Dual Wield after soft discount ==== If Eviscerate discounted by {{C|Bullet Time}}, {{R|Mummified Hand}}, unupgraded {{C|Enlightenment}}, or generated by {{C|Foreign Influence}}, {{P|Attack Potion}}, {{C|Discovery}} is played as a {{C|Nightmare}} target or {{C|Dual Wield}} target, it will return at its original Snecko Eye {{Icon|GE}} cost '''on the same turn'''. == Update History == * '''Patch V2.2: Happy Holidays!''' ** Eviscerate card buffed. Damage increased from 6 -> 7. ** Eviscerate+ card buffed. Damage increased from 8 -> 9. * '''Weekly Patch 45: Impatience''' ** Fixes for how Eviscerate incorrectly worked with cost reduction effects like Enlightenment. * '''Weekly Patch 25: Building Blocks''' ** Eviscerate card now has correct cost when returned from Stasis power. * '''Weekly Patch 13: Thinking Ahead''' ** Eviscerate now correctly lowers cost by 1 per discard. * '''Weekly Patch 9: Ascension''' ** Fixed interaction of Enlightenment + Eviscerate + Discard. * '''Weekly Patch 6: We're Back!''' ** Eviscerate's cost now correctly decreases when it is discarded. * '''Weekly Patch 2: Slimes!''' ** Eviscerate now correctly works with the Confusion debuff. {{SilentNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
* The {{Icon|BE}} Energy generated by Fusion's {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orb}} allows for playing expensive and X cost cards, such as {{C|Echo Form}}, {{C|Meteor Strike}}, {{C|Tempest}}, {{C|Reinforced Body}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}}.

==== General Orb Synergies ====
* Other Orb sources, such as {{C|Darkness}} and {{C|Coolheaded}}, can be very helpful for {{KW|Evoke|Evoking}} {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} more frequently.
* Sources of additional Orb Slots allow for having more [[Orbs#Passive|Orb Passives]] in parallel: {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, {{P|Potion of Capacity}}
* {{C|Compile Driver}} draws a card for each unique type of Orb {{KW|Channel|Channeled}}.
* {{C|Barrage}} deals damage for each {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} Orb, while {{C|Fission}} draws a card and adds 1 {{Icon|BE}} for each Channeled Orb.
* {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}} each can directly {{KW|Evoke}} your Orbs 1, 2, or X times respectively.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* As {{BD|Focus}} has no effect on {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}}, {{C|Consume}} removing an Orb Slot is a strict downside for {{KW|Plasma}}.

* The artwork for Fusion appears to depict a {{KW|Plasma}} Orb being formed by combining {{KW|Lightning}}, {{KW|Frost}}, and {{KW|Dark}} Orbs.

{{C|Havoc}} is a 1 (0 if upgraded) {{Icon|RE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Red|Ironclad}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Common|Common}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} Card. It plays and {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausts}} the top card of your draw pile, without expending any {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy'''. X-cost cards will use your current {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy''' for X, without consuming that {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy'''.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* The top card being played and being {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} are separate, meaning the resolution of the played card takes place ''before'' any results of {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausting}} that card can occur.
** This means that {{BD|Beat of Death}} will trigger ''before'' {{C|Feel No Pain}} gives {{KW|Block}} as a result of the card being {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} by {{C|Havoc}}.

=== Synergies ===
* {{C|Headbutt}}, {{C|Warcry}} and {{C|Thinking Ahead}} let you manipulate the top card of your draw pile, giving you more control over {{C|Havoc}}.
* {{R|Frozen Eye}} allows you to see which card {{C|Havoc}} will target.

=== Neutral ===
* If your draw pile is empty when playing {{C|Havoc}}, it will shuffle your discard pile into your draw pile and target the new top card.
* {{R|Strange Spoon}} has a 50% chance of saving a card that would be {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} by {{C|Havoc}}.

== Update History ==
* '''Patch V2.0: The Watcher'''
** Fixed Mayhem, Havoc, Distilled Chaos, and Omniscience sometimes not playing cards if original target is dead.

* '''Weekly Patch 54: Loop'''
** Tingsha, Sword Boomerang, Bouncing Flask, Rip and Tear, Thunder Orbs, Havoc, and Juggernaut now utilize seeded enemy target randomization.

* '''Weekly Patch 51: Recursion'''
** Accuracy power now correctly works with Shivs played from the top of the deck via cards like Mayhem or Havoc.

* '''Weekly Patch 35: Aggregate'''
** Fix for crash when playing Havoc against half dead enemies (Darkling/Awakened one).

* '''Weekly Patch 33: Terror'''
** Havoc card now utilizes RNG to select its random target (save/load consistency).

* '''Weekly Patch 23: Testing Continues'''
** Havoc card's description: Exhaust was not capitalized.

* '''Weekly Patch 3: Balance Balance Balance'''
** Havoc can now be played even when no cards are in your deck. (Discard will shuffle in)

== Obtaining Impatience ==
{{C|Impatience}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card, and therefore can be obtained in the following ways:
* Can be bought from the [[Merchant]].
* Can appear in the {{E|Sensory Stone}} event, from a choice of 3-9 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards, depending on the option that is selected.
* Can be obtained from Neow's [[First Blessing]] via the {{TS|green||'''Obtain an Uncommon Colorless Card'''}} bonus.
* Can be obtained from [[Monsters]] and [[Elites]] with {{R|Prismatic Shard}}.
** Also found in the [[Custom Mode|Daily Climb]] with the {{KW|Diverse}} or {{KW|Colorless Cards}} modifiers.
* Can be obtained from the {{Frame|Success?}} option at {{E|Knowing Skull}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
* Synergizes well with hand-management through for example {{KW|Exhaust}} or [[Keywords#Discard|Discard]] effects.
* When drawing it through {{R|Unceasing Top}}, the only card in hand will be {{C|Impatience}}, meaning it can be played.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* As opposed to most cards and strategies in this game, this card pairs poorly with effects that allow you to draw cards, except for previously mentioned {{R|Unceasing Top}}. 
* It pairs poorly with {{R|Dead Branch}}, since {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausting}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} cards is a way to enable you to play {{C|Impatience}}, but this can possibly replace those cards with other {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} cards.

{{C|Injury}} is an {{KW|Unplayable}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} Card.

== Obtaining Writhe ==
Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Injury can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse:
* Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward.
* {{E|Match and Keep}}.
* {{R|Cursed Key}}.
* {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse.

In addition, Injury can be obtained from the {{E|Golden Idol}} Event when choosing {{Frame|Take}} and then {{Frame|Outrun}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
As Injury is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following:
* {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn.
* {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat.
* {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. 
* When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Injury, it cannot be played.

== Trivia ==
Injury can be seen as the Curse equivalent of the {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Status}} {{C|Wound}}, with both being the most basic penalty cards of their respective types.

Given that {{C|Lesson Learned}} {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausts}} after use, it synergizes with: ** {{R|Strange Spoon}}, which gives a 50% chance to not {{KW|Exhaust}} {{C|Lesson Learned}} when played, allowing it to be redrawn and used again. ** {{C|Exhume}}, which can get {{C|Lesson Learned}} back once after being played, with the added benefit of putting it directly into your hand. * {{C|Lesson Learned}} can mitigate the downside of {{R|Fusion Hammer}}, as it often fully upgrades your deck over time. * As you have less need to use [[Map Locations#Rest_Sites|Rest Sites]] for upgrading, {{R|Girya}}, {{R|Peace Pipe}} and {{R|Shovel}}, the relics that give alternate actions at [[Rest Site|Rest Sites]], become better. === Neutral === * When duplicated through an effect such as {{C|Double Tap}} or a {{P|Duplication Potion}}, {{C|Lesson Learned}} will trigger its {{KW|Fatal}} effect even if only the second play was {{KW|Fatal}}. ** As duplicated {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}} always target the same enemy with both plays, you cannot trigger {{C|Lesson Learned}} twice by duplicating it. * {{KW|Fatal}} does ''not'' trigger when {{BD|Minion|Minions}} are killed. ** However, the {{M|Cultist}} enemies in {{M|Awakened One}} fight are not technically {{BD|Minion|Minions}}, and ''can'' trigger {{KW|Fatal}}. * {{KW|Fatal}} is not affected by {{M|Slime Boss}} or other Slime enemies splitting, and only triggers when reducing a Slime's health to 0, whether that Slime was spawned as the result of a split or not. * The first phase of {{M|Awakened One}} does not trigger {{KW|Fatal}}, but the second phase does. * In the {{M|Darkling|Three Darklings}} fight, an attack is only considered {{KW|Fatal}} if it kills the last {{M|Darkling}};
