== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* As {{BD|Like Water}} gives {{KW|Block}} at the end of your turn, it does not prevent {{R|Orichalcum}} from activating.

=== Synergies ===
* Depends on being in {{KW|Calm}}, meaning it synergizes with ways to enter that {{KW|Stance}}:

==== Cards ====
* {{C|Vigilance}} can reliably make you enter {{KW|Calm}}.
* {{C|Tranquility}} can make you enter {{KW|Calm}} once at any point after first drawing it, making it a good fallback.
* {{C|Fear No Evil}} cannot reliably make you enter {{KW|Calm}}. However, in most cases the {{KW|Block}} from {{BD|Like Water}} is only needed if there is an enemy attacking, in which case this does work.
* {{C|Inner Peace}} synergizes well, as it allows you to enter {{KW|Calm}} and still receive full benefits from itself while remaining in {{KW|Calm}}.
* {{C|Meditate}} reliably ensures you are in {{KW|Calm}} at the end of your turn.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Teardrop Locket}} makes you start combat in {{KW|Calm}}.
* {{P|Stance Potion}} allows you to pick between entering {{KW|Calm}} and {{KW|Wrath}}.

=== Neutral ===
* The {{KW|Block}} gained by {{BD|Like Water}} is unaffected by {{BD|Frail}}, {{BD|Dexterity}} or {{BD|No Block}} from a previously played {{C|Panic Button}}.

{{C|Mayhem}} is a 2 (1 if upgraded) {{Icon|CE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives one {{BD|Mayhem}}, which plays the top card of your draw pile at the start of every turn, without expending any {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy'''. X-cost cards will use your current {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy''' for X, without consuming that {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy'''.

== Obtaining Mayhem ==
{{C|Mayhem}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card, and therefore can be obtained in the following ways:
* Can be bought from the [[Merchant]].
* Can appear in the {{E|Sensory Stone}} event, from a choice of 3-9 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards, depending on the option that is selected.
* Can be obtained from [[Monsters]], [[Elites]] and [[Bosses]] with {{R|Prismatic Shard}}.
** Also found in the [[Custom Mode|Daily Climb]] with the {{KW|Diverse}} or {{KW|Colorless Cards}} modifiers.
* Can be obtained from Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a negative effect.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{BD|Mayhem}} activates ''after'' drawing cards at the start of the turn, meaning that something that is placed on top of your draw pile at the end of your previous turn will not be played through {{BD|Mayhem}} but drawn as normal.
* If you have {{BD|Echo Form}}, the card played by {{C|Mayhem}} will be played twice by that {{BD|Echo Form}} and consume it for that turn.

=== Synergies ===
* {{R|Frozen Eye}} allows you to see which card {{C|Mayhem}} will target.
* {{C|Mayhem}} will play X-cost cards for their full {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy''' without actually using any.

=== Neutral ===
* Playing a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Status}} card via {{BD|Mayhem}} will place the card into your discard pile, bypassing end-of-turn negative effects from cards such as {{C|Doubt}} and {{C|Burn}}, but also preventing {{KW|Ethereal}} cards such as {{C|Ascender's Bane}} and {{C|Dazed}} from being {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}}.
** If you have {{R|Medical Kit}} or {{R|Blue Candle}}, respectively {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Status}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} will be {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} when they are played by {{BD|Mayhem}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* Generally, there is little control over which card is played by {{BD|Mayhem}}. This means cards with possible negative effects, such as {{C|Offering}}, {{C|Eruption}} or {{C|Blasphemy}} can be played, or cards that need to be played at a specific time for maximum effect, such as {{C|Limit Break}} or {{C|Apparition}} can be wasted.

It gives 4 (6 if upgraded) {{BD|Mental Fortress}}, which gives that amount of {{KW|Block}} every time you switch {{KW|Stance}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* When changing your {{KW|Stance}} as a result of a card, {{BD|Mental Fortress}} will activate before the card is fully resolved, meaning it can already {{KW|Block}} damage such as from {{BD|Beat of Death}}.

=== Synergies ===
* Anything that can cause you to switch {{KW|Stance}} will synergize with this card:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Empty Body}}, {{C|Empty Fist}} and {{C|Empty Mind}}, as long as you were in a {{KW|Stance}} previously.

* As long as you were not in {{KW|Wrath}} previously, {{C|Eruption}}, {{C|Crescendo}}, {{C|Indignation}}, {{C|Simmering Fury}} and {{C|Tantrum}}.

*  As long as you were not in {{KW|Calm}} previously, {{C|Vigilance}}, {{C|Tranquility}}, {{C|Fear No Evil}}, {{C|Inner Peace}} and {{C|Meditate}}.
** {{C|Fear No Evil}} will only work if it is played on a target that [[Intent|Intends]] to attack.

* As long as you were not in {{KW|Divinity}} previously, {{C|Prostrate}}, {{C|Pray}}, {{C|Worship}} and {{C|Devotion}} can give you enough {{BD|Mantra}} to enter {{KW|Divinity}}, and {{C|Blasphemy}} can do it directly.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Damaru}} can give you enough {{BD|Mantra}} to enter {{KW|Divinity}}.
* {{P|Stance Potion}} will always give you the possibility to switch {{KW|Stance}}, no matter what your current {{KW|Stance}} is.
* As long as you were not in {{KW|Divinity}} previously, {{P|Ambrosia}}.

=== Neutral ===
* The {{KW|Block}} gained by {{BD|Mental Fortress}} is unaffected by {{BD|Frail}}, {{BD|Dexterity}} or {{BD|No Block}} from a previously played {{C|Panic Button}}.

Luckily, [[Defect]] has various ways to produce a lot of {{Icon|BE}} Energy: ** {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} ** {{C|TURBO}} ** {{C|Recycle}} ** {{C|Double Energy}} ** {{C|Aggregate}} ** {{C|Fission}} * In addition, as {{R|Snecko Eye}} can only make cards cost up to 3, it will ''always'' reduce the cost of Meteor Strike. * Once Meteor Strike has been played once, the {{Icon|BE}} from the {{KW|Plasma}} Orbs it generates makes playing it again much easier. * {{C|Meteor Strike}} gets a damage increase from {{R|Strike Dummy}} and adds to the damage of {{C|Perfected Strike}}. * Meteor Strike is a particularly good target for {{R|Necronomicon}} and {{C|Echo Form}}. Assuming you have 3 Orb Slots, the second copy will {{KW|Evoke}} the Orbs generated by the first copy, immediately repaying 6 {{Icon|BE}} while doing substantial damage. * Due to its high cost, Meteor Strike is a good target for {{C|Recycle}}, if you don't need to play it in a given combat. * The {{Icon|BE}} Energy generated by Meteor Strike's {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} allows for playing other expensive and X cost cards, such as {{C|Echo Form}}, {{C|Tempest}}, {{C|Reinforced Body}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}}. ==== General Orb Synergies ==== * Other Orb sources, such as {{C|Darkness}} and {{C|Coolheaded}}, can be very helpful for {{KW|Evoke|Evoking}} {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} more frequently. * Sources of additional Orb Slots allow for having more [[Orbs#Passive|Orb Passives]] in parallel: {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, {{P|Potion of Capacity}} * {{C|Compile Driver}} draws a card for each unique type of Orb {{KW|Channel|Channeled}}. * {{C|Barrage}} deals damage for each {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} Orb, while {{C|Fission}} draws a card and adds 1 {{Icon|BE}} for each Channeled Orb. * {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}} each can directly {{KW|Evoke}} your Orbs 1, 2, or X times respectively. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{BD|Focus}} has no effect on {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}}, {{C|Consume}} removing an Orb Slot is a strict downside for {{KW|Plasma}}. == Trivia == * Not counting X-cost cards or {{C|Masterful Stab}}, both of which can be played for arbitrarily large amounts of Energy, Meteor Strike is the most expensive card in the game. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 28: The Ritual''' ** Fixed issue where Strike (blue), Thunder Strike, and Meteor Strike weren't used by Perfected Strike. * '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World''' ** This week adds the long anticipated third character into the game! ** A new character with unique mechanics, keywords, and art. ** Content: 75 Cards. {{DefectNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

Moreover, unlike {{C|Ascender's Bane}} and {{C|Curse of the Bell}}, it cannot be {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} mid-combat either; doing so will immediately conjure another copy of the '''Curse''' into your hand. == Obtaining Necronomicurse == '''Necronomicurse''' is obtained when you pick up {{R|Necronomicon|The Necronomicon}} from the {{E|Cursed Tome}} event. == Interactions == === Order === * When {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}}, '''Necronomicurse''' returns to your hand ''after'' {{KW|Exhaust}} triggers happen. ** If your hand is full and you have {{R|Dead Branch}} or {{C|Dark Embrace}} in play, '''Necronomicurse''' will be unable to be added to your hand, as it is full again, and will go to your '''Discard Pile''' instead. === Synergies === As '''Necronomicurse''' is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal '''6(10)''' damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you '''+1''' {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for '''1 HP'''. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you '''6 max HP''' if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. In addition, '''Necronomicurse''' can be {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} repeatedly, allowing cards such as {{C|Burning Pact}}, {{C|Sever Soul}}, and {{C|Second Wind}} to use it for value repeatedly. === Infinite === Due to '''Necronomicurse''''s unique ability to {{KW|Exhaust}} repeatedly, it can be used in some unusual '''infinites'''. Late in [[Custom Mode#Endless|Endless]] runs, the addition of the [[Blight]] {{R|Time Maze}} prevents you from playing more than '''15''' ''non-Curse'' cards in one turn. The intent of the '''Blight''' appears to be to remove '''infinite''' combos as an option, while not penalizing the player for {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausting}} {{C|Pride}}. However, due to this exception to the rule, the above '''infinites''' eventually become the ''only'' viable '''infinites''' in [[Custom Mode#Endless|Endless Mode]]. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as '''Necronomicurse''', it cannot be played. == Trivia == * At the event {{E|N'loth}}, offering '''N'loth''' {{R|Necronomicon}} will remove exactly 1 copy of '''Necronomicurse'''. If the '''Curse''' was duplicated by {{E|Duplicator}} or {{R|Dolly's Mirror}}, you keep the other copies. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 1|* Necronomicurse no longer shows up on card removal screens (since it cannot be removed).}} {{Update History Table/row|?|* Added Necronomicurse to the game}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

While it is in your hand, you can only play up to 3 cards in a turn. == Obtaining Normality == Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Normality can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse: * Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward. * {{E|Match and Keep}}. * {{R|Cursed Key}}. * {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse. In addition, Normality can be obtained from the {{E|Mind Bloom}} Event when choosing {{Frame|I am Rich}}. == Interactions == === Order === * Normality only prevents further card plays while actively in the hand. If, for instance you draw and then discard it in a single card play, such as with {{C|Acrobatics}} or {{C|Scrape}}, your turn can continue as normal. * As drawing for the turn happens before {{C|Mayhem}}, Normality can prevent Mayhem from playing more than 3 cards. === Synergies === As Normality is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. ** However, doing so counts as playing a card, so you can only do this if you've played less than 3 cards so far this turn. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. Normality's unique downside is often very problematic. However, some effects can mitigate the downside: * It can be discarded away with {{C|Acrobatics}}, {{C|Survivor}}, {{C|Prepared}}, {{C|Dagger Throw}}, {{C|Calculated Gamble}}, {{C|All-Out Attack}}, {{C|Concentrate}}, {{C|Storm of Steel}}, {{C|Tools of the Trade}}, {{C|Unload}}, {{R|Gambling Chip}}, and {{P|Gambler's Brew}}. * In addition to Blue Candle, it can be {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} with {{C|Havoc}}, {{C|True Grit}}, {{C|Burning Pact}}, {{C|Second Wind}}, {{C|Sever Soul}}, {{C|Fiend Fire}}, {{C|Purity}}, and {{P|Elixir}}. * {{R|Pocketwatch}} can draw you additional cards after a turn where you end up stuck with Normality in your hand. === Neutral === * Drawing into Normality after playing more than 3 cards in a turn has no additional effect; it simply shuts off further card plays as usual. * Multiple copies of Normality do not stack; you can still only play 3 cards in a turn. * Double playing a card by any means ({{P|Duplication Potion}}, {{C|Echo Form}}, etc.) counts as '''two plays''' for all purposes. If the second play would be your fourth card for the turn, the card will not be played. * Cards played by {{P|Distilled Chaos}} and similar effects are still counted for Normality. If such an effect would go past 3 card plays for the turn, the remainder will simply be discarded. * The effect of Normality is '''not a [[Debuff]]''', and cannot be bypassed with {{BD|Artifact}} or {{R|Orange Pellets}}. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Normality, it cannot be played. * {{C|Regret}} and Normality synergize in a harmful fashion; only being able to play 3 cards means there are more cards left in your hand when Regret goes off. * Cards that generate lots of {{C|Shiv|Shivs}}, such as {{C|Blade Dance}}, {{C|Cloak and Dagger}}, and {{C|Storm of Steel}} tend to be dangerous to play with Normality in hand, as you take your entire turn for one card and/or end up shuffling Shivs into your deck. * Cards that generate Energy when played, and especially those that draw cards as well, are likely to be wasted due to Normality: {{C|Offering}}, {{C|Doppelganger}}, {{C|Adrenaline}}, and {{C|Fission}}. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|V1.1|* Fixed exploit of playing Normality while already having played 3+ cards. * Fixed Normality card not stopping cards affected by Setup and Forethought.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 41|* Accursed Blacksmith's curse penalty reduced from Normality -> Pain.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 33|* Normality card's reminder text no longer uses incorrect wording.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 6|* Clarification for Normality. {{C|Noxious Fumes}} is a 1 {{Icon|GE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy's turn, it has some unusual interactions:
* If the damage is enough to cause {{M|The Guardian}} to change to Defensive form, it will immediately change its [[Intent]] to apply {{BD|Sharp Hide}}. Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn.
** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected.
* If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn.
** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn.
* If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn.
* If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking.

=== Synergies ===
* {{C|Bane}} does additional damage if the target has {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Catalyst}} can double (triple) the amount of {{BD|Poison}} on a target.
* {{R|The Specimen}} can be used in combats with multiple enemies to consolidate {{BD|Poison}} as enemies die.
* {{R|Snecko Skull}} applies 1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever this card applies {{BD|Poison}}.

* {{C|Noxious Fumes}} works well with other sources of {{BD|Poison}}:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Poisoned Stab}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}}, {{C|Crippling Cloud}}, {{C|Noxious Fumes}}, {{C|Corpse Explosion}}, {{C|Envenom}}.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Twisted Funnel}}.
* {{P|Poison Potion}}.

=== Neutral ===
* {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process.
* {{BD|Poison}} bypasses {{KW|Block}} and {{BD|Flying}}.
* However, {{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{BD|Artifact}} will prevent applying {{BD|Poison}}. {{BD|Noxious Fumes}} will naturally clear out {{BD|Artifact}} over time.
* Certain bosses will remove all [[Debuffs]] during combat: {{M|The Champ}}, {{M|Awakened One}}, and {{M|Time Eater}}.

== Update History ==

** Updating icon for Noxious Fumes power.

{{C|Panache}} is a 0 {{Icon|CE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It applies the {{BD|Panache}} effect on the player, which does 10 (14) damage to ALL enemies every time you play 5 cards in one turn. This effect can trigger more than once per turn, so for instance playing 10 cards in one turn will cause the damage to occur twice.

== Obtaining Panache ==
{{C|Panache}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card, and therefore can be obtained in the following ways:
* Can be bought from the [[Merchant]].
* Can appear in the {{E|Sensory Stone}} event, from a choice of 3-9 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards, depending on the option that is selected.
* Can be obtained from [[Monsters]], [[Elites]] and [[Bosses]] with {{R|Prismatic Shard}}.
** Also found in the [[Custom Mode|Daily Climb]] with the {{KW|Diverse}} or {{KW|Colorless Cards}} modifiers.
* Can be obtained from Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a negative effect.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
Regardless of character, there exist ways to play infinite cards in a single turn, which naturally synergizes with Panache. As there are many different ways to go infinite, and most infinites generate damage even without Panache, for the rest of this section only finite strategies are listed.

==== As the Ironclad ====
[[Ironclad]] usually does not play very many cards in a turn, and so will rarely be able to proc Panache. 
* {{C|Corruption}} makes all Skills cost 0, allowing more cards to be played most turns.
* {{C|Offering}} and {{C|Seeing Red}} both generate {{Icon|RE}}, and may allow playing more cards in a turn.

==== As the Silent ====
[[Silent]] tends to play many cards at once fairly easily, and generally benefits the most from Panache.
* {{C|Shiv}} generation cards, especially {{C|Blade Dance}} and {{C|Storm of Steel}}, enable playing 5 cards for very little {{Icon|GE}}.
* {{C|Adrenaline}}, {{C|Concentrate}}, {{C|Outmaneuver}}, {{C|Flying Knee}} and {{C|Tactician}} all give you access to more Energy.
* {{C|Bullet Time}} makes your whole hand cost 0 temporarily.
* {{C|Choke}} does not directly enable more card plays, but it also benefits from many cards being played at once.

==== As the Defect ====
[[Defect]] primarily benefits from Panache when either using a 0-cost strategy or [[Orbs#Plasma Orbs|Plasma Orbs]].
* {{C|All for One}} and {{C|Scrape}} enable playing lots of 0 cost cards in a single turn.
* Sources of Plasma allow you to consistently have more {{Icon|BE}} each turn: {{C|Fusion}}, {{C|Meteor Strike}}, {{C|Chaos}}, and {{R|Nuclear Battery}}.
* Defect also has various other Energy generation methods: {{C|Double Energy}}, {{C|Aggregate}}, {{C|Fission}}, {{C|Recycle}}, and {{C|TURBO}}.

==== As the Watcher ====
[[Watcher]] has quite a lot of ways to generate both cards that cost 0 and {{Icon|PE}} (thanks in part to both {{KW|Calm}} and {{KW|Divinity}}).
* Sources of {{C|Miracle}}s: {{C|Collect}}, {{C|Deus Ex Machina}}, and {{R|Pure Water}}.
* Sources of {{KW|Scry}} allow you to manipulate your hand, avoiding drawing dead cards: {{C|Third Eye}}, {{C|Foresight}}, and {{C|Cut Through Fate}}.
* {{C|Scrawl}} gives you access to many cards at once.
* {{C|Deva Form}} gives you a huge amount of Energy as combat goes on, enabling lots of card plays per turn consistently.

==== All Classes ====
* {{C|Enlightenment}} and {{C|Madness}} both reduce the cost of cards potentially allowing playing more cards per turn.
* {{C|Purity}} allows you to exhaust several cards at will, allowing the removal of {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Statuses}} or unwanted cards like {{C|Strike (Ironclad)|Strike}}, allowing you to draw cheap cards more consistently.

==== Relics ====
* Any relic which gives Energy.
* {{R|Unceasing Top}} allows you to continuously draw more cards to play, assuming you have energy left.
* {{R|Mummified Hand}} makes cards temporarily free when playing Powers.
* Various relics benefit from playing lots of cards as well: {{R|Ornamental Fan}}, {{R|Letter Opener}}, {{R|Ink Bottle}}.

=== Neutral ===
==== Strength ====
Is completely unaffected by {{BD|Strength}}. This means the debuff from [[Spire Spear]] will have no effect on it, but neither will {{R|Shuriken}}, {{R|Vajra}}, or {{C|Inflame}}.

==== Thorns and Flight ====
As Panache does not do Attack damage, it bypasses {{M|Spiker|Spikers'}} {{BD|Thorns}} and {{M|Byrd|Byrds'}} {{BD|Flying}}, but it also does not benefit from {{M|Giant Head|Giant Head's}} {{BD|Slow}}.

==== Stances ====
Similarly, the damage from Panache is not affected by being in {{KW|Wrath}} or {{KW|Divinity}}. However, the Energy generated by entering Divinity may make it easier to proc the damage in the first place.

If Parasite is {{KW|Transform|Transformed}} or [[Merchant#Card Removal Service|Removed]] from your deck, you will lose 3 Max HP immediately. == Obtaining Parasite == Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Parasite can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse: * Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward. * {{E|Match and Keep}}. * {{R|Cursed Key}}. * {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse. In addition, Parasite can be obtained from both the {{E|Hypnotizing Colored Mushrooms}} Event and the {{M|Writhing Mass}} fight. It is the only card in the game which can be added to your deck permanently mid-combat. == Interactions == === Synergies === As Parasite is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. ** Note that Exhausting Parasite does ''not'' trigger the Max HP loss. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. Ways to gain more Max HP repeatedly will make the downside of removing Parasite minimal: * {{C|Feed}} can gain you Max HP when you kill enemies with it. * {{R|Singing Bowl}} can gain you Max HP whenever you skip a card reward. Somewhat counterintuitively, reducing your Max HP once can make other Max HP reduction Events slightly better, as most Events that reduce your Max HP do so as a percentage of your current Max HP. * For instance, say you have 75 Max HP, and then remove a Parasite, leaving you with 72 HP. Then, you encounter the {{E|Council of Ghosts}} Event, which allows you to pay half of your Max HP for 5 ({{Asc|15|3}}) copies of {{C|Apparition}}. From 72 Max HP, this would be a payment of 36 Max HP, for a total of 39 Max HP lost. If instead you had not removed the Parasite, you would be asked to pay 38 Max HP, only 1 less total, while keeping the Curse. === Neutral === Like all sources of Max HP loss, Parasite: * Won't affect your current HP, unless you have less HP than your new Maximum, in which case it will also lower to the same amount. * Cannot lower your Max HP below 1. If it would, it sets it to 1 instead. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Parasite, it cannot be played. * While it is often still worthwhile to remove Parasite with things such as {{R|Empty Cage}}, doing so will reduce your Max HP by 3. == Trivia == * As most Curses are only given in a single Event (not counting random ones), Parasite is tied with {{C|Writhe}} and {{C|Regret}} for being the Curse with the most ways to get it. * {{M|Writhing Mass}} is the only thing in the game which can permanently add a card to your deck mid combat. In addition, there are a number of ways to affect your game state in a lasting way mid combat ({{C|Hand of Greed}}, {{C|Alchemize}}), but they are nearly all player-controlled. The only enemies which can cause such things to happen (aside from HP loss) are Writhing Mass and the {{M|Looter}} and {{M|Mugger}}, who can steal your [[Gold]]. * This card's [[Beta Art]] shows the parasite causing the terrible affliction of :3 to the [[Ironclad]], [[Silent]], and [[Defect]]. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 44|* Mushroom event now correctly shows card preview for Parasite curse.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 17|* Ascender's Bane: Replaces Parasite for Ascension 10. * Ascension 10 now gives you Ascender's Bane rather than Parasite.}} {{Update History Table/row|?|* Added Parasite to the game}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

On pickup, three copies of Pride are added to your deck. == Interactions == === Order === * {{R|Nilry's Codex}} happens ''before'' Pride. Any copies of Pride generated at end of turn will necessarily be on top of the deck. * Pride happens ''before'' [[Orbs#Passive|Orb Passives]]. So, if a {{KW|Lightning}} Orb kills an enemy while you have {{R|Gremlin Horn}}, you will draw the newly generated Pride before discarding for the turn. ** As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy turn (rather than the end of your turn), if the enemy dies to Poison you will draw the generated Pride, and keep it until your next turn. === Synergies === As Pride is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}. === Neutral === * Normally, {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} would gain you max HP on picking up Pride. However, under normal circumstances you cannot obtain Pride until after four loops of Endless mode; on the third loop, you will receive {{R|Muzzle}}, which prevents increasing your max HP any more. So, in practice Darkstone Periapt no longer does anything by the time you get to Pride. * Despite the stated in game phrasing, only non-Curse cards are counted towards {{R|Time Maze|Time Maze's}} 15 card limit. Playing copied of Pride therefore does not count towards this limit. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Pride, it cannot be played. * Unlike with other Curses, which normally can't be played, {{R|Blue Candle}} actually gives a downside with Pride. Playing Pride will still cost {{Icon|CE}}, but it will ''also'' cost 1 HP. == Bugs == === Pandora's Box Skip === ''Main article: [[Pandora's Box#Pandora's Box Skip]]'' Picking up Pride may be skipped using an exploit with the game's menu. * On Desktop: ** Receive your Grotesque Trophy, so you are on the screen where you can confirm adding the copies of Pride to your deck. ** Open up the game menu, then hit "Abandon Run", but '''do not confirm'''. ** Hit the Escape key twice, bypassing the card pickup. * On Mobile or Desktop: ** Receive your Grotesque Trophy, so you are on the screen where you can confirm adding the copies of Pride to your deck. ** Open up the game menu, then hit "Abandon Run", but '''do not confirm'''. ** Click on the menu gear icon again, then hit the "Return" button. This bypasses the card pickup, allowing you to continue past Neow. == Trivia == * Pride is the only Curse which can be {{KW|Transform|Transformed}}, but not Transformed into. * Pride's [[Beta Art]] references the fact that pride also refers to a group of lions. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 31|* Pride curse will no longer appear from Calling Bell and a few other sources.}} {{Update History Table/row|?|* Added Pride to the game}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

It deals 4 (5 if upgraded) damage to '''ALL''' enemies and heals you for the amount of unblocked damage it dealt. You will only heal for the amount of HP actually lost by the enemy, so killing an enemy with damage remaining will only heal you for the HP they had left. {{C|Reaper}} will then {{KW|Exhaust}} itself. == Interactions == === Order === * The healing from {{C|Reaper}} takes effect ''after'' receiving damage from {{BD|Thorns}} or {{BD|Sharp Hide}}, but before taking damage from {{BD|Beat of Death}}. === Synergies === * {{R|Magic Flower}} increases the effectiveness of any healing from {{C|Reaper}}. * Any increase to the damage output of {{C|Reaper}} will also boost its healing: ** {{BD|Vulnerable}} on any of the enemies, particularly with {{R|Paper Phrog}}. ** Any positive amount of {{BD|Strength}}. ** {{BD|Vigor}}. ** {{R|The Boot}} boosting its unblocked damage to 5. ** Being in the {{KW|Wrath}} or {{KW|Divinity}} {{KW|Stance}}. === Neutral === * Healing cards cannot be generated mid-combat to avoid infinite healing, so {{C|Reaper}} cannot be created by {{C|Infernal Blade}}, {{C|Metamorphosis}} or {{R|Dead Branch}}. ** However, if you already have a {{C|Reaper}} cards can be generated that allow you to heal to full HP regardless: *** Sources of {{BD|Strength}}, like {{C|Spot Weakness}} or {{C|Demon Form}}. *** Ways to increase the amount of {{C|Reaper|Reapers}} played, like {{C|Dual Wield}} or {{C|Exhume}}. === Anti-Synergies === * {{C|Reaper}} suffers doubly from any penalty to its damage, meaning {{BD|Weak}} and negative {{BD|Strength}} are particularly harmful for this card. * {{C|Reaper}} relies on damaging enemies at the right moment, meaning that damage that you have no control over, such as from {{C|Combust}}, {{BD|Thorns}} or {{R|Stone Calendar}} can possibly reduce the healing you get from this card. == Bugs == * '''Reaper''' can sometimes fail to heal under certain circumstances. * After lethal damage is dealt, combat will be ended after 1 second when updateDeathAnimation concludes that enemies are done dying. '''Reaper's''' heal action is added to the bottom of the queue and a WaitAction is added to the top. If additional actions take long enough, '''Reaper's''' heal will never be reached before combat is ended. ** This is most noticeable combats with multiple enemies, like {{M|Reptomancer}}, with delays like {{R|Charon's Ashes}}. == Trivia == * The {{M|Jaw Worm}} and {{M|Red Louse}} are depicted in the card art. == Update History == * '''Patch V1.1: The Dealer''' ** Improved lifesteal logic for Reaper and Shelled Parasite. * '''Weekly Patch 55: Blur''' ** Reaper card now heals the correct amount if the player has The Boot relic. ** Adding VFX for Reaper card. * '''Weekly Patch 44: Chrysalis''' ** All sources of random temporary card generation in combat (like Dead Branch) can no longer generate cards that provide healing. ** New tip added to indicate that healing cards cannot be generated randomly during combat. * '''Weekly Patch 6: We're Back!''' ** Reaper now heals as part of the attack now, not after (you heal before thorns hit you). {{IroncladNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

If this card is discarded from your hand, draw (2;3) cards. |GivesToPlayer = Draw, Discard, Unplayable }} {{C|Reflex}} is an unplayable {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. == Interactions == === Synergies === * Reflex does nothing unless [[Keywords#Discard|discarded]], in one of the following ways: ==== Cards ==== * {{C|Survivor}}, {{C|Acrobatics}}, {{C|Dagger Throw}}, {{C|Prepared}}, {{C|Calculated Gamble}}, {{C|Concentrate}}, {{C|Tools of the Trade}},{{C|Storm of Steel}}, {{C|Unload}}. * {{C|All-Out Attack}}, although this cannot reliably target {{C|Reflex}}. * {{C|Scrape}}. ==== Relics and potions ==== * {{R|Gambling Chip}}. * {{P|Gambler's Brew}}. == Trivia == * Under normal circumstances, Reflex is the only card in the game which can directly draw itself. title: Regret
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox |Name = Regret |Image = Curse-Regret.png |Color = Colorless |Type = Curse |Cost = -2 |NoUpgrade = true |Description = {{KW|Unplayable}}.
At the end of your turn, lose HP equal to the number of cards in your hand. |GivesToPlayer = Unplayable }} {{Keyword Infobox|Unplayable}} {{C|Regret}} is an {{KW|Unplayable}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} Card. If it is in your hand at end of turn, it will cause you to lose HP equal to the amount of cards still in your hand. This counts the number of cards in your hand at the time you press the End Turn button, and so includes Regret itself. This card will also forcibly [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] itself at the end of its turn, even if you {{KW|Retain}} it or have {{R|Runic Pyramid}}. == Obtaining Decay == Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Regret can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse: * Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward. * {{E|Match and Keep}}. * {{R|Cursed Key}}. * {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse. In addition, Regret can be obtained from both the {{E|Big Fish}} Event when choosing the {{Frame|Box}} and {{E|Golden Shrine}} when choosing {{Frame|Desecrate}}. == Interactions == === Order === * Regret will discard itself at the end of your turn before the rest of your hand, at the same time it applies the HP loss. This happens ''before'' {{KW|Retain}} happens, so you cannot choose to Retain it. * '''Regret''', {{C|Decay}}, {{C|Burn|Burns}}, {{C|Shame}}, and {{C|Doubt}} all activate at the same time at end of turn. Visually they activate from left to right. However: ** Regardless of the order of activation, Regret counts any copies of the others as being still in your hand when its damage is applied. *** Regret does ''not'' take into account cards drawn from {{R|Runic Cube}} as a result of taking damage from these cards; it will always just use the number of cards in your hand when your turn ended. ** If Regret, {{C|Decay}}, or {{C|Burn}} cause you to draw into any of the above via {{R|Runic Cube}}, those newly drawn cards will ''not'' go off, and will be discarded with the rest of your hand. ** The damage for Regret, {{C|Burn}}, and {{C|Decay}} are applied from left to right. So, if you have 1 stack of {{BD|Buffer}} and two of them in hand, the left one will have its damage consumed, and the right one will apply. *** When selecting cards from your hand, such as to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] or {{KW|Exhaust}}, you can freely reorder your hand, as selecting and then unselecting a card moves it to the last spot in your hand. If needed, this can be used to manipulate which card's damage is applied to you. === Synergies === As Regret is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. The HP loss from Regret can be: * Negated with {{BD|Buffer}}, via {{R|Fossilized Helix}} and {{C|Buffer}}. * Reduced to 1 with {{BD|Intangible}}, via {{R|Incense Burner}}, {{C|Wraith Form}}, and {{C|Apparition}}. * Reduced by 1 with {{R|Tungsten Rod}}. The HP loss from Regret can also be used to your benefit: * Losing HP causes {{R|Runic Cube}} to draw you a card. * {{C|Blood for Blood}} will have its cost reduced for the rest of combat. * The HP loss is counted as being from a card, so {{C|Rupture}} will gain you {{BD|Strength}}. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Regret, it cannot be played. * Losing HP from Regret causes {{C|Masterful Stab}} will have its cost increased for the rest of combat. == Trivia == * As most Curses are only given in a single Event (not counting random ones), Regret is tied with {{C|Writhe}} and {{C|Parasite}} for being the Curse with the most ways to get it. * This card's [[Beta Art]] references the fact that {{M|Byrd|Byrds}} become significantly more dangerous with {{BD|Strength}} due to its {{Int|Byrd|Peck}} move. {{R|Philosopher's Stone}} gives enemies 1 {{BD|Strength}}, which doubles {{M|Byrd|Byrds'}} damage output. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|V1.1|* Fixed Regret causing less HP loss than normal if other cards played themselves first.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 50|* Regret card wording improved to clarify interactions with cards like Rupture.}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 10|* Fixed issue where Regret/Decay/Doubt/Burn fails to exhaust via Blue Candle and Medical Kit.}} {{Update History Table/row|?|* Added Regret to the game}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) {{BD|Rupture}}, which gives that amount of {{BD|Strength}} whenever a card causes you to lose HP. == Interactions == === Order === * {{C|Hemokinesis}} will not benefit from the {{BD|Strength}} gained as a result of {{BD|Rupture}} until played again, as {{BD|Rupture}} triggers ''after'' the card is already resolved. * HP loss caused by {{C|Pain}} applies ''after'' the effects of the card that triggered it, meaning {{BD|Rupture}} will trigger ''after'' the card that triggered {{C|Pain}} has already dealt damage. ** However, if you have {{C|Pain}} in hand and use a different card to cause an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} to be played, such as through {{C|Havoc}}, the first card will trigger {{C|Pain}} and therefore {{BD|Rupture}} ''before'' the {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} takes effect. === Synergies === * Playing any {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} with {{R|Blue Candle}} triggers {{BD|Rupture}}. * {{C|Reaper}} gives healing based on damage dealt, and therefore increases with {{BD|Strength}}. This can be used to regain HP lost as a result of triggering this card. * Any card that can cause you to lose HP can trigger {{BD|Rupture}}: ==== Cards ==== * {{C|Bloodletting}}, {{C|Hemokinesis}} and {{C|J.A.X.}} can repeatedly be played to trigger it. * {{C|Offering}} can be played to trigger it and then {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausts}}. * {{C|Combust}} and {{C|Brutality}} will trigger it every turn. * {{C|Regret}} will trigger it if it is in your hand at the end of your turn. * {{C|Pain}} makes every other card in hand cost 1 HP, allowing you to rack up large quantities of {{BD|Strength}} quickly. * {{C|Burn}} and {{C|Decay}} deal damage instead of causing HP loss directly. This will still trigger {{BD|Rupture}}, as long as the damage is not fully negated by {{KW|Block}}, and therefore causes you to lose HP. === Neutral === * The amount of {{BD|Strength}} gained from triggering {{BD|Rupture}} does not scale with the amount of HP lost. * Losing HP when playing a card, as a result of {{BD|Thorns}}, {{BD|Sharp Hide}} or {{BD|Beat of Death}}, will not trigger {{BD|Rupture}}. == Trivia == * Technically {{C|Blasphemy}} deals 99999 damage instead of killing the player directly. In theory this could be used to activate {{C|Rupture}}, although unpractical in reality. == Update History == * '''Patch V2.2: Happy Holidays!''' ** Rupture+ card buffed. Strength gain increased from 1 -> 2. ** Rupture+ card nerfed. Energy cost 0 -> 1. * '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot''' ** Updating icon for Rupture power. {{IroncladNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

It gives 2 {{BD|Rushdown}}, which makes you draw that amount of cards whenever you enter the {{KW|Wrath}} {{KW|Stance}}, as long as you were not in {{KW|Wrath}} before.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* If you enter {{KW|Wrath}} because of a card, that card will be placed into the discard pile, or draw pile in the case of {{C|Tantrum}}, before {{BD|Rushdown}} is triggered, meaning it is possible to immediately redraw that card.

=== Synergies ===
* Depends on being in {{KW|Wrath}}, meaning it synergizes with ways to enter that {{KW|Stance}}:

==== Cards ====
* {{C|Eruption}}, {{C|Indignation}} and {{C|Tantrum}} can reliably make you enter {{KW|Wrath}}.
* {{C|Crescendo}} can make you enter {{KW|Wrath}} once at any point after first drawing it, making it a good fallback.
* {{C|Simmering Fury}} triggers after you draw the start of your turn, and gives extra draw on top of that, meaning this has a high chance of already filling your hand before {{BD|Rushdown}} can be useful.

==== Potions ====
* {{P|Stance Potion}} allows you to pick between entering {{KW|Calm}} and {{KW|Wrath}}.

== Trivia ==
* During beta testing Rushdown was called Adaptation, and triggered on all Stance changes. The internal name is still Adaptation.

wikitext:

If it is in your hand at end of turn, it will [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] itself, and apply 1 {{BD|Frail}} to you. == Obtaining Shame == Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Shame can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse: * Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward. * {{E|Match and Keep}}. * {{R|Cursed Key}}. * {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse. In addition, Shame can be obtained from the {{E|Pleading Vagrant}} Event when choosing {{Frame|Rob}}. == Interactions == === Order === * Shame will discard itself at the end of your turn before the rest of your hand, at the same time it applies the {{BD|Frail}}. This happens ''before'' {{KW|Retain}} happens, so you cannot choose to Retain it. * Shame, {{C|Doubt}}, {{C|Regret}}, {{C|Decay}}, and {{C|Burn|Burns}} all activate at the same time at end of turn. Visually they activate from left to right. However: ** Regardless of the order of activation, {{C|Regret}} counts any copies of the others as being still in your hand when its damage is applied. ** For Shame and {{C|Doubt}}, the [[Debuffs]] are applied from left to right. So, if you have 1 stack of {{BD|Artifact}} and both in hand, the left one will consume the Artifact and the right one will apply. *** When selecting cards from your hand, such as to [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] or {{KW|Exhaust}}, you can freely reorder your hand, as selecting and then unselecting a card moves it to the last spot in your hand. If needed, this can be used to manipulate which Curse's debuff is applied to you. === Synergies === As Shame is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' Omamori. The {{BD|Frail}} debuff can be dealt with in a few ways: * It can be prevented with sources of {{BD|Artifact}}, such as {{C|Core Surge}} and {{C|Panacea}}. * It can be removed during your next turn with {{R|Orange Pellets}}. * The downside can be ignored by having a {{KW|Block}} plan that doesn't require Block cards, such as {{C|After Image}}, {{C|Apparition}}, {{C|Wraith Form}}, {{KW|Frost|Frost Orbs}}, or {{C|Buffer}}. * {{C|Barricade}} can carry {{KW|Block}} between turns, reducing the impact of a single turn of {{BD|Frail}}. * {{C|Vault}} can be used to skip to your next turn, clearing the debuff without giving the enemy a chance to attack first. === Neutral === * Shame cannot be {{KW|Retain|Retained}}, and does not stay in your hand with {{R|Runic Pyramid}}, as it discards itself as part of its end of turn activation. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Shame, it cannot be played. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Weekly 38|* Adding curse card Shame.}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

{{C|Simmering Fury}} is a 1 {{Icon|PE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Purple|Watcher}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives you one {{BD|Simmering Rage}}, which will make you enter the {{KW|Wrath}} {{KW|Stance}} at the start of your next turn. It also gives 2 (3 if upgraded) {{BD|Draw Card}}, which will make you draw that amount of extra cards at the start of next turn.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{BD|Simmering Rage}} activates after {{BD|Mantra}} is given at the start of your turn. This means that if you get enough {{BD|Mantra}} to enter {{KW|Divinity}} through {{C|Devotion}} or {{R|Damaru}}, you will briefly enter {{KW|Divinity}} and then immediately enter {{KW|Wrath}}. This will give you the 3 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''' benefit from entering {{KW|Divinity}}, and counts as two {{KW|Stance}} switches.

* {{BD|Draw Card}} will activate after drawing cards regularly at the start of your turn, and after any possible {{BD|Rushdown}} draws cards as a result of having entered {{KW|Wrath}} through {{BD|Simmering Rage}}. This means that having excess {{BD|Draw Card}} will end up simply being wasted.

=== Synergies ===
* When entering {{KW|Wrath}} if you are not in {{KW|Wrath}} yet:
** If you have {{BD|Rushdown}} from {{C|Rushdown}}, you will draw that many cards.
** You will switch {{KW|Stance}}, which results in the following:
*** Any {{C|Flurry of Blows}} that was in your discard pile will be brought back to your hand, as long as there is space in hand.
*** {{C|Mental Fortress}} will give {{KW|Block}}.
*** If you were in the {{KW|Calm}} {{KW|Stance}} before, you will gain 2 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''', or 3 if you have {{R|Violet Lotus}}.

* Being in {{KW|Wrath}} changes the effects of some cards:
** {{C|Halt}} will give its additional {{KW|Block}}.
** {{C|Indignation}} will apply {{BD|Vulnerable}}.

=== Neutral ===
* While in {{KW|Wrath}}, all {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} damage you deal is doubled, but you also take double damage from enemy attacks.{{KW|Wrath}} only doubles damage from {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, not from effects such as {{BD|Panache}} or {{BD|Thorns}}, or relics such as {{R|Mercury Hourglass}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* As {{KW|Wrath}} is worse than the {{KW|Divinity}} {{KW|Stance}} in every way except for the aformentioned ones, using {{C|Simmering Fury}} while in {{KW|Divinity}} is generally bad.

== Trivia ==
* In the game code, Simmering Fury is called Vengeance.

* Static Discharge will {{KW|Channel}} the Orb ''immediately'' upon receiving the damage, before the enemy turn can continue. This can {{KW|Evoke}} Orbs in the middle of an attack:
** If a {{KW|Lightning}} or {{KW|Dark}} Orb is Evoked, the damage can kill an enemy. If it is the enemy currently attacking, it will die immediately, ending the attack even if there were additional hits remaining. 
*** If an enemy dies this way while you have {{R|Gremlin Horn}} (and the combat does not end), you will receive {{Icon|BE}} and draw cards after the current attack has concluded. The cards will be kept until your next turn, while the {{Icon|BE}} will be lost unless you have {{R|Ice Cream}}.
** If a {{KW|Frost}} Orb is Evoked, the {{KW|Block}} will be applied immediately. This will reduce subsequent damage, even if those are further hits of the same attack. 
** If a {{KW|Plasma}} Orb is Evoked, the {{Icon|BE}} it generates will be lost, unless you have {{R|Ice Cream}}.

=== Synergies ===
* Static Discharge is particularly effective in fights with multi-hit attacks, especially including [[Hexaghost]], [[Byrd|Byrds]], [[Book of Stabbing]], and the [[Corrupt Heart]]
* {{R|Torii}} and {{R|Tungsten Rod}} can both decrease the amount of damage you receive while still allowing Static Discharge to trigger.

==== General Orb Synergies ====
* Other Orb sources, such as {{C|Darkness}} and {{C|Coolheaded}}, can be very helpful for {{KW|Evoke|Evoking}} {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} more frequently.
* {{C|Thunder Strike}} hits more times for each {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orb}} {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} this combat, and {{C|Electrodynamics}} makes {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} hit all enemies.
* Sources of {{BD|Focus}} will improve the effects of Orbs: {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Consume}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, {{R|Data Disk}}
* Sources of additional Orb Slots allow for having more [[Orbs#Passive|Orb Passives]] in parallel: {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, {{P|Potion of Capacity}}
* {{C|Bullseye}} applies {{BD|Lock-On}}, which makes damaging Orbs deal 50% more damage to that enemy.
* {{C|Compile Driver}} draws a card for each unique type of Orb {{KW|Channel|Channeled}}.
* {{C|Barrage}} deals damage for each {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} Orb, while {{C|Fission}} draws a card and adds 1 {{Icon|BE}} for each Channeled Orb.
* {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}} each can directly {{KW|Evoke}} your Orbs 1, 2, or X times respectively.

=== Neutral ===
* Static Discharge will only {{KW|Channel}} Orbs when taking attack damage. Other sources of enemy damage such as {{BD|Thorns}} and {{BD|Beat of Death}} will not trigger it.
* Static Discharge requires you to actually take damage to trigger: if an enemy is doing 0 damage (perhaps due to having negative {{BD|Strength}}), it will not trigger even if you have 0 {{KW|Block}}.
** Similarly, damage prevented with {{BD|Buffer}} will not trigger Static Discharge.
** However, as {{R|Tungsten Rod}} reduces ''HP Loss'', rather than damage, it is possible to lose no HP while triggering Static Discharge, if the attack would have done precisely 1 unblocked damage.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, making {{KW|Lightning}} Orbs less effective.

Static Discharge card now clarifies that it triggers when you receive unblocked attack damage.

title: Vault

{{Card Infobox |Name = Vault |Image = Purple-Vault.png |Color = Purple |Type = Skill |Rarity = Rare |Cost = 3 |CostPlus = 2 |Description = Take an extra turn after this one.

It ends your turn, and skips every part of the enemy's turn, as well as the end of the round, bringing it immediately to the start of your turn again. == Interactions == === Order === * Anything that triggers, decreases or wears off at any part of your turn still functions as normal, for example: ** Your {{KW|Block}} is removed as normal. ** Any form of {{KW|Retain}}, such as through {{BD|Retain Cards|Well-Laid Plans}} or {{BD|Equilibrium}} triggers, as well as {{BD|Establishment}} reducing the cost of these {{KW|Retain|Retained}} cards. ** Effects such as {{BD|Double Tap}}, {{BD|Rebound}} and {{BD|Entangled}} wear off. ** You will lose {{BD|Strength}} or {{BD|Dexterity}} through effects such as {{BD|Strength Down}} or {{BD|Wraith Form}}. ** You will exit the Divinity {{KW|Stance}}. ** Damaging effects, such as {{BD|Omega}} or {{BD|The Bomb}} deal damage as normal. * Anything that triggers, decreases, wears off or resets at any point of the enemy's turn is skipped. ** Anything mentioned in the previous block is skipped if it belongs to an enemy instead of the player. ** Enemies keep their {{KW|Block}} ** [[Byrd|Byrds]] do not reset their {{BD|Flying}} and the [[Corrupt Heart]] does not reset its {{BD|Invincible}} * Anything that triggers, decreases, wears off or resets at the end of the round is skipped. ** {{BD|Frail}}, {{BD|Vulnerable}}, {{BD|Weak}} and {{BD|Lock-On}} do not decrease. ** {{BD|Blur}}, {{BD|Double Damage}}, {{BD|Equilibrium}}, {{BD|Intangible}}, and {{BD|No Block}} do not decrease, although their effects still apply as normal. ** {{BD|Draw Reduction}}, {{P|Duplication Potion}}, and {{BD|Wave of the Hand}} do not wear off, although their effects still apply as normal. ** A [[Cultist]]'s {{BD|Ritual}} and a [[Orb Walker]]'s {{BD|Strength Up}} do not trigger. ** {{BD|Malleable}} and {{BD|Slow}} do not reset. == Interactions == === Synergies === * Synergizes with {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} that trigger every turn, for example {{C|Deva Form}}'s {{BD|Deva}} will scale. * Scales any {{C|Perseverance}}, {{C|Sands of Time}}, and {{C|Windmill Strike}} that is {{KW|Retain|Retained}}. * {{C|Vault}} can be used to negate the forced end of turn of {{BD|Time Warp}} if played as the 12th card, as well as the card limit of {{R|Velvet Choker}} or {{C|Normality}}. === Anti-Synergies === * Playing this card twice through an effect like {{C|Omniscience}} or a {{P|Duplication Potion}} will result in that effect being wasted, as the first copy played already ends your turn, preventing the second play. * {{BD|Draw Reduction}} applies but does not wear off, meaning playing {{C|Vault}} while having this debuff makes it affect you twice. * {{C|Blasphemy}}'s {{BD|Blasphemer}} will trigger immediately. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 10|* Adding VFX for Vault card.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 6|* Vault card description updated to clarify its effect.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 5|* Reworked Vault card.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 1|* Added Vault to the game ''(likely)''}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{WatcherNav}} When playing an X {{Icon|RE}}-cost card, all {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy''' that you currently have will be consumed. The {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy''' consumed this way will be used as the value for X.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
* Benefits X times from {{BD|Strength}} or {{BD|Vigor}}.

* If {{C|Whirlwind}} is used with 2 or more {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy''', it will be able to trigger {{R|Necronomicon}}.
* If played using {{P|Distilled Chaos}}, {{C|Havoc}}, or {{C|Omniscience}}, it will play for the full current {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy''' without actually using any.
* Can be used with 0 {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy''' to advance {{R|Ink Bottle}}, {{R|Nunchaku}}, {{R|Kunai}}, {{R|Shuriken}}, and {{R|Ornamental Fan}}.

=== Neutral ===
* If {{C|Whirlwind}} is duplicated with an effect such as a {{P|Duplication Potion}} or {{C|Double Tap}}, the value of X will also be used for the copy.
* Being an X-cost, {{C|Whirlwind}} can be targeted by {{C|Recycle}} to double the current {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy'''.
* It will not count as a 0-cost card for {{C|All for One}} or {{C|Scrape}}, even with {{C|Swivel}}'s {{BD|Free Attack Power}} active.

See [[#Interactions|Interactions]] below. * {{BD|Dexterity}} sources such as {{C|Footwork}} and potentially {{C|Reprogram}} or {{C|Fasting}} can be used to temporarily counteract ongoing {{BD|Dexterity}} reduction from {{BD|Wraith Form}}. * {{BD|Intangible}} provided from {{C|Apparition}} will stack on top of any {{BD|Intangible}} gained through {{C|Wraith Form}}. * {{C|Wraith Form}} is a strong {{C|Nightmare}} target, giving the player access to substantially more stacks of {{BD|Intangible}}. However, playing '''X''' {{C|Wraith Form|Wraith Forms}} causes the {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff to stack, reducing '''X''' {{BD|Dexterity}} each turn. * {{C|Well-Laid Plans}} can be used to {{KW|Retain}} {{C|Wraith Form}} until an optimal turn, such as an especially high-damage enemy attack, to maximise damage reduction. * Self-damage cards such as {{C|Offering}} and {{C|Hemokinesis}} will only reduce the player's HP by 1 while {{BD|Intangible}} is active. === Relics === * {{R|Tungsten Rod}} reduces all HP loss to 0 while the player has {{BD|Intangible}}. * Sources of {{BD|Dexterity}} such as {{R|Kunai}} and to a lesser extent {{R|Oddly Smooth Stone}} can also counteract the {{BD|Dexterity}} loss induced by {{BD|Wraith Form}}. * The {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff can be '''entirely cleansed''' using {{R|Orange Pellets}}. Since {{C|Wraith Form}} is itself a Power, playing an Attack and a Skill the same turn as it will activate {{R|Orange Pellets}} and clear all debuffs, including {{BD|Wraith Form}}. * The {{BD|Artifact}} provided by {{R|Clockwork Souvenir}} at the start of combat can be used to nullify the {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff. Since the relic always activates at the very start of combat, its {{BD|Artifact}} will always nullify {{BD|Wraith Form}} entirely when {{C|Wraith Form}} is played instead of doing so for just one turn (see [[#Interactions|Interactions]]). === Potions === * {{P|Ancient Potion}} can provide {{BD|Artifact}}, which will nullify the {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff if used ''before'' {{C|Wraith Form}} is played (see [[#Interactions|Interactions]] below). * {{P|Dexterity Potion}} can temporarily counteract the {{BD|Dexterity}} loss induced by {{BD|Wraith Form}}. * {{P|Ghost in a Jar}} can also provide 1 stack of {{BD|Intangible}} (2 with {{R|Sacred Bark}}) which is additive with {{BD|Intangible}} gained from {{C|Wraith Form}}. === Power-based === Being a Power, it will: * '''Heal''' for '''2''' with {{R|Bird-Faced Urn}}. * Make a random card cost 0 temporarily with {{R|Mummified Hand}}. * Draw '''X''' cards with '''X''' stacks of {{C|Heatsinks}}. * Generate '''X''' {{Icon|LO}} '''Lightning Orbs''' with '''X''' stacks of {{C|Storm}}. == Interactions == === Artifacts === {{BD|Artifact}} can be used to prevent the {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff, but will only cleanse the debuff in full if acquired ''before'' {{C|Wraith Form}} is played. If '''X''' {{BD|Artifact}} is acquired ''after'' the player already has the {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff, the next '''X''' instances of {{BD|Dexterity}} loss will be prevented, but the debuff itself will not be cleansed. This interaction applies regardless of how {{BD|Artifact}} is gained, whether through cards, relics, or potions. === Thorns and Beat of Death === * While {{BD|Intangible}}, [[Corrupt Heart]]'s {{BD|Beat of Death}} deals only 1 damage each time a card is played. * [[Guardian]]'s {{BD|Sharp Hide}} and [[Shapes#Spiker|Spikers]]' {{BD|Thorns}} will only deal 1 damage while {{BD|Intangible}} is active. === Other sources of Intangible === Acquiring {{BD|Intangible}} through other means, such as {{C|Apparition}} or {{P|Ghost in a Jar}}, will increment {{BD|Intangible}} stacks provided by {{C|Wraith Form}} and vice versa. === Enemy intents === If an enemy is attacking while the player has {{BD|Intangible}}, their intent will be updated to show 1 damage per hit. Multi-hits will be converted to 1 times X damage, where X is the number of hits the enemy intends to inflict. === Sources of Block unaffected by Dexterity === The {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff has no effect on sources of {{KW|Block}} that do not scale with {{BD|Dexterity}}. These include: * {{P|Block Potion}} * {{C|After Image}} * {{C|Feel No Pain}} * {{C|Mental Fortress}} * {{C|Nirvana}} * {{C|Like Water}} * {{KW|Frost|Frost Orbs}} * {{R|Ornamental Fan}} * {{R|Orichalcum}} * {{R|Anchor}}, {{R|Horn Cleat}}, and {{R|Captain's Wheel}}. == Trivia == * {{C|Wraith Form}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, and {{C|Fasting}} are the only Power cards in the game that afflict the player with a '''persistent''' debuff. {{C|Berserk|Berserk's}} {{BD|Vulnerable}} debuff is capped at 2 turns (1 if upgraded). * {{C|Wraith Form|Wraith Form's}} Beta Art was prominently featured on the [https://contentiongames.myshopify.com/products/slay-the-spire-beta-art-cards Beta Art expansion box] of [https://contentiongames.com/games/slay/ Slay the Spire: The Board Game]. {{SilentNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

It is {{KW|Innate}}. == Obtaining Writhe == Like most {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}}, Writhe can be obtained from anything that gives a random Curse: * Can be part of Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a reward. * {{E|Match and Keep}}. * {{R|Cursed Key}}. * {{KW|Transform|Transforming}} another Curse. In addition, Writhe can be obtained from two events: * {{E|The Mausoleum}} when choosing {{Frame|Open Coffin}}. * {{E|Winding Halls}} when choosing {{Frame|Pass On}}. == Interactions == === Synergies === As Writhe is a '''{{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}}''', it interacts with the following: * {{C|Fire Breathing}} will deal damage when it is drawn. * {{R|Du-Vu Doll}} will give you 1 {{BD|Strength}} each combat. * {{R|Blue Candle}} can be used to {{KW|Exhaust}} it for 1 HP. * When added to the deck, it will be negated by {{R|Omamori}}, or gain you 6 max HP if you have {{R|Darkstone Periapt}} and ''not'' {{R|Omamori}}. As Writhe is '''{{KW|Innate}}''', the downside of having it can be mitigated: * {{R|Gambling Chip}} allows you to discard it away at the start of combat, meaning you won't draw it until after the first shuffle. * {{R|Ring of the Snake}} and {{R|Bag of Preparation}} both draw you additional cards on your first turn, lessening the impact of an Innate curse in your starting hand. === Anti-Synergies === * As {{C|Clash}} can only be played when all cards in your hand are {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, if it is drawn at the same time as Writhe, it cannot be played. == Trivia == As most Curses are only given in a single Event (not counting random ones), Writhe is tied with {{C|Parasite}} and {{C|Regret}} for being the Curse with the most ways to get it. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|?|* Added Writhe to the game}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{No Update History}} {{ColorlessNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

== Obtaining Zap ==
The [[Defect]] starts the game with one copy of Zap in their deck.

Zap cannot be obtained through regular card rewards, but can be obtained in the {{E|Match and Keep}} Event. 

If you already have Zap in your deck, it can be duplicated using {{R|Dolly's Mirror}} or the {{E|Duplicator}} Event.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
==== General Orb Synergies ====
* Other Orb sources, such as {{C|Darkness}} and {{C|Coolheaded}}, can be very helpful for {{KW|Evoke|Evoking}} {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} more frequently.
* {{C|Thunder Strike}} hits more times for each {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orb}} {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} this combat, and {{C|Electrodynamics}} makes {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} hit all enemies.
* Sources of {{BD|Focus}} will improve the effects of Orbs: {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Consume}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, {{R|Data Disk}}
* Sources of additional Orb Slots allow for having more [[Orbs#Passive|Orb Passives]] in parallel: {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, {{P|Potion of Capacity}}
* {{C|Bullseye}} applies {{BD|Lock-On}}, which makes damaging Orbs deal 50% more damage to that enemy.
* {{C|Compile Driver}} draws a card for each unique type of Orb {{KW|Channel|Channeled}}.
* {{C|Barrage}} deals damage for each {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} Orb, while {{C|Fission}} draws a card and adds 1 {{Icon|BE}} for each Channeled Orb.
* {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}} each can directly {{KW|Evoke}} your Orbs 1, 2, or X times respectively.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, making {{KW|Lightning}} Orbs less effective.
